routes.name: Alta Trail
routes.desc: A maintained trail climbs from Wolverton through forest to Panther Gap, then across a meadow and past Tharps Rock to switchbacks on the summit. Long day with about 4,000 feet of gain.

routes.name: Northeast Buttress
routes.descent: Head down toward the saddle separating Banner from Ritter, where both sides hold snow, so carry an ice axe. From the saddle, glissade the snow slope below it back toward the lakes.

routes.name: Standard route
routes.desc: Class 3 to the summit block, which is Class 4.

routes.name: West Slope from Black Giant Pass
routes.desc: A remote peak reached off the John Muir Trail near Muir Pass; leave the trail for Black Giant Pass, then walk up about half a mile of loose rock to the summit. The east-side approach over Echo Col from Lake Sabrina adds class 3 and possible snow.

routes.name: Via Summit Creek and Mosquito Pass
routes.desc: Follow Summit Creek trail about 10 miles to Lunch Meadow, leave the trail before Mosquito Pass, and climb a drainage to the summit ridge.

routes.name: Via Taboose Pass
routes.desc: Hike the Taboose Pass trail about eight miles to the pass, then climb the peak about a mile to the north. The south chute is loose; the solid rock nose to its right is a more pleasant way up.

routes.name: Standard route
routes.desc: Class 2 to the summit block, which is Class 3.

routes.name: Via Castle Pass
routes.desc: Take the Pacific Crest Trail under I-80 to Castle Pass, then follow the ridge northeast to the top of the northwest turret. The last bit is a loose, steep scramble. Class 2 to the summit block, which is Class 3.

routes.name: After Party
routes.descent: Rappel the route from the belay anchors, which have rappel rings.

routes.name: Standard route
routes.desc: Class 2 to the summit block, which is Class 4.

routes.name: Northeast Ridge
routes.desc: From a high camp, follow the south side of the northeast ridge, crossing snow patches and then rock. Near the top a traverse leads to a narrow chute and a notch below the summit monolith.

routes.name: Rock Route
routes.descent: along the ridge toward the neighbouring spire, one 10-ft class 4 section, then down the north-side chute to the ledge across the face

routes.name: Via Coyote Pass and the Saddle
routes.desc: A very long approach: from the trailhead go over Farewell Gap, south along the trail to Coyote Pass, then cross-country to the saddle between the two summits. A short boulder scramble finishes the climb. Water can be scarce on the trail.

routes.name: Via Clover Meadow
routes.desc: Follow the Pacific Crest Trail north about five miles to Clover Meadow, then leave it and climb roughly 3,000 ft west through dense manzanita to the ridge. The true highpoint is the northern rock group, a short distance beyond the lower southern summit, with some class 3 on the ridge.

routes.name: Regular Northwest Face of Half Dome
routes.descent: Walk off the top by the cable route and follow the main hiker trail roughly 8 miles down to the valley floor. If the cables are not up for the season, the lowered cables can still be handled hand over hand. Take care on the cables, and expect close to four hours for the hike out.

routes.name: Northeast Buttress
routes.desc: Cross Kearsarge Pass, descend to Bubbs Creek, and head up Vidette Creek cross-country. Climb the northeast buttress to the lower northwest summit and traverse to the high point.

routes.name: Southwest Ridge
routes.desc: Follow the trail past two meadows to a faint side trail, then leave it near 8,800 ft and go cross-country over sage slopes to the southwest ridge. The summit hump is steep talus.

routes.name: Southeast Slopes from Virginia Lakes
routes.desc: Leave the parking area cross-country up the southeast slopes, cross low scrub, then slog talus to the broad plateau and the summit. Easy terrain overall but the talus is loose.

routes.name: Standard route
routes.desc: Class 2 to the summit block, which is Class 3.

routes.name: West Gully to North Ridge
routes.desc: Reach the Evolution Meadow area via the John Muir Trail, then climb the broad west-face gully to the north ridge and follow it to the top. Rock is loose; exit the gully to the south after the second tower to avoid class 3.

routes.name: South Ridge via Tahoe Rim Trail
routes.desc: Hike up toward Armstrong Pass, join the Tahoe Rim Trail, and follow the Freel Peak trail up the sandy ridge to the summit. Several trail approaches exist, all non-technical.

routes.name: Standard route
routes.desc: Class 2 to the summit block, which is Class 4.

routes.name: Via Grouse Lake and Northwest Ridge
routes.desc: Follow the Copper Creek Trail to the Granite Basin area, then go cross-country to Grouse Lake. Climb to the saddle between Munger Peak and Goat, then follow the northwest ridge to the summit. Long day with a lot of gain.

routes.name: West Side from Taboose Pass
routes.desc: Climb the Taboose Pass trail, go into the basin left of the summit ridge, and reach the saddle between Goodale and Striped Mountains. Scramble the steep slope to the southern pinnacle; only the last 20 ft are third class. Class 2 to the summit block, which is Class 3.

routes.name: Granite Chief Trail from Olympic Valley
routes.desc: Take the trail from behind the fire station along the ski area boundary to the Pacific Crest Trail, then follow the northeast ridge to the summit.

routes.name: Standard route
routes.desc: Class 2 to the summit block, which is Class 5.

routes.name: Via Noble Lake
routes.desc: Follow the Pacific Crest Trail to Noble Lake, then a use trail to the saddle and class 2 sand to the summits.

routes.name: Via Fern Lake
routes.desc: Cross the San Joaquin River and take the Mammoth Trail and Beck Lakes Trail to Fern Lake, then climb scree to the ridge and the summit pyramid. About 7 miles each way, partly off-trail.

routes.name: Kern Peak Trail (East Face)
routes.desc: A long, mostly trail approach through the Kern Plateau meadows leads to a gentle cross-country finish up the east face. Sandy trail sections can be hard to follow.

routes.name: Via Parker Pass and Koip Peak Pass
routes.desc: Follow the Mono Pass trail to the Parker Pass junction, cross Parker Pass, and climb switchbacks on Parker Peak's north flank to Koip Peak Pass. From there, a short walk-up over talus leads to the summit.

routes.name: Lamont Peak Trail
routes.desc: A short, steep trail climbs the ridge from the Canebrake Road saddle, fades in places, then follows cairns up the final ridge to the summit rocks. Expect a bit of scrambling and boulder hopping near the top.

routes.name: Pacific Crest Trail and East Shoulder
routes.desc: Follow the PCT south from Sonora Pass, leave it at a notch on the ridge, and continue up the talus ridge to the broad summit area.

routes.name: Bastille Buttress - Beckey Route
routes.descent: The route tops out on a ledge system on the back of the buttress. Scramble the ledges up and left on the backside, cross the crest onto the east side, and scramble down the long gully of scree that runs beside the buttress on the left; there are other gullies, so confirm the right one in daylight. The gully ends at the Inyo Creek drainage, where a trail leads back toward the road. A longer alterna

routes.name: Bastille Buttress - Papillon
routes.descent: The route joins the Beckey line near the top and finishes at the same ledge system on the back of the buttress. Scramble the ledges up and left on the backside, cross the crest to the east side and descend the long scree gully beside the buttress on the left to the Inyo Creek drainage. The gully is loose, and the correct one should be identified in daylight.

routes.name: Direct South Face
routes.descent: From the plateau at the top, head east toward the large knob, pass it on its left side and aim for the sharp east ridge. Keep the ridge on your left and follow the broad gully down toward Tuttle Creek, staying left at junctions; the ground is sand and shrubs and there are no cairns or trail. routes.name: Land of Little Rain
routes.descent: After topping out, the descent goes by the east ledges to Tuttle Creek. Head east from the top with the sharp east ridge on your left and follow the broad gully down toward the creek. Before reaching the creek, bear up and leftward toward a low saddle on the ridge at your left; if you miss it you end up in dense brush. From the saddle, sand or snow leads to the dirt road along the creek's north ba

routes.name: North Ridge (full)
routes.descent: From the summit, hike southwest down to the plateau and cross it to the west-facing scree gully that leads toward Grass Lake. Several gullies look alike from above, so identify it beforehand. Snow or ice may remain in it early in the season. Below Grass Lake, join the Meysan Lakes trail and follow it down to the Whitney Portal campground.

routes.name: Standard route
routes.descent: Return across the summit plateau to the head of the wide chute you came up, a west-facing scree gully that is easy to confuse with its neighbours, so note it on the way up. The gully is steep scree and talus, and early-season snow can lie in the upper part, so an ice axe may be worth carrying. routes.name: Michael Strassman Memorial Route
routes.descent: From the top of the fifth pitch or the bolted station at the bush, the choices are to rappel the route with two 60 m ropes to the notch, or to continue to the summit. To continue, follow the summer ridge up and left, or go from the top of the fifth pitch up the Land of Little Rain line to a broken roof and a large crack near the ridge, then follow the ridge and join the Direct South Face to the to

routes.name: NE Ridge (full)
routes.descent: Two descents are used. The east ledges descent goes down the sandy class 2 slopes with the east ridgeline in view, avoiding the steep cliffs to the south and southeast by contouring left whenever they feel close. routes.name: North Ridge
routes.descent: From the summit, hike southwest down to the plateau and cross it until you find a west-facing scree gully; several gullies look alike from above, and picking the wrong one is the usual mistake, so check the line from the valley beforehand. Once you are in the right one, the whole line down is visible. Early in the season, or after a big winter, the gully may hold snow or ice that calls for an ice

routes.name: Winter Route
routes.descent: Once on the plateau, or after visiting the summit, locate the east ridge and descend alongside it, keeping it to your left, until a broad gully opens. Descend it directly toward Tuttle Creek. About five hundred vertical feet above the creek, traverse up and leftward to a low saddle on the ridge at your left, and study the saddle from the approach road beforehand. Carrying on straight down the gull

routes.name: Northeast Ridge
routes.desc: Reach Cartridge Pass or Marion Lake, then follow the northeast ridge on class 2 terrain.

routes.name: East Couloir
routes.descent: The normal way down is the approach route: reverse the couloir (snow in winter and spring, loose scree and a mixed scramble by late summer), cross the glacier edge and drop the moraine ridge to the lake and the Horse Creek Trail. From the top of the couloir the summit is reached by third-class ledges on the east ridge or by traversing round to the easier south side, so downclimb the same ground. A

routes.name: West Slope
routes.desc: A multi-day approach reaches the Colby Lake area in Cloud Canyon. From there a class 2 slope leads up to the summit.

routes.name: North Ridge
routes.desc: Cross Kearsarge Pass, leave the trail near the Charlotte Lake junction, and go west cross-country into the cirque below the peak. Climb a chute to the easy north ridge and follow it to the summit.

routes.name: Via Convict Canyon and Bright Dot Lake
routes.desc: Follow the trail up from Convict Lake to Bright Dot Lake, then a use trail up the steep sand and gravel above it to the summit. About 13 miles round trip with roughly 5,000 ft of gain.

routes.name: Standard route
routes.desc: Class 2 to the summit block, which is Class 3.

routes.name: Dana Couloir
routes.descent: trail from the summit down to Tioga Pass

routes.name: Southeast Slopes from North Glacier Pass
routes.desc: Walk to Thousand Island Lake and North Glacier Pass, then up easy slopes. The hard part is picking the true summit among bumps.

routes.name: Southeast Ridge from Black Rock Pass
routes.desc: Cross Glacier Pass and descend toward Cliff Creek, climb to Black Rock Pass, then traverse the ridge to the saddle at the base of the southeast ridge. Follow the ridge to the summit; long and tedious rather than hard.

routes.name: Mt. Elwell Trail
routes.desc: A trail leads up from the Lakes Basin to the summit. Other access points also exist.

routes.name: West Ridge from Lucys Foot Pass
routes.desc: Approach via the Bubbs Creek and East Lake drainage to Lake Reflection and the chute leading to Lucys Foot Pass, then scramble the west ridge to the summit. A multi-day trip with exposed, loose terrain near the top.

routes.name: Guyot Pass Route
routes.desc: Reach the Pacific Crest Trail near Guyot Pass from Horseshoe Meadow, then climb the sandy slopes to the broad summit plateau. A short blocky summit block needs a few scrambling moves.

routes.name: West Ridge
routes.desc: Follow the trail past Post Corral Creek to Fleming and Lower Indian lakes, then go cross-country up grassy slopes to the west ridge and along it to the top. About 2 miles and 2,000 ft past the lake.

routes.name: Southwest Ridge via Tombstone Pass
routes.desc: Follow Tombstone Creek to Tombstone Pass, traverse to the cirque below the summit and climb the southwest ridge to the summit block. The block itself is a short 5.4 crack on the south side. Class 2 to the summit block, which is Class 4.

routes.name: East Face
routes.desc: Hike the Mono Creek trail to Mott Lake, go cross-country to Bighorn Lake, and climb the mostly solid east face. Descend the sandy south face.

routes.name: Standard route
routes.desc: Class 3 to the summit block, which is Class 4.

routes.name: South Face
routes.descent: scree chute, a handy way down

routes.name: Christine
routes.descent: From the top, either walk off or rappel. For the walk-off, go left (south and southeast) over third and fourth class ground to the high point of the ridge, then trend down and left along ledges to easier ground. routes.name: Mindy
routes.descent: There are no bolted anchors or bail points on the route, so the way off is up and over. From the top, follow the ridge toward the summit of Lamarck, then descend easily toward Lamarck Col and join the col trail in the neighbouring basin. routes.name: Nicole
routes.descent: From the top, either walk off or rappel. routes.name: North Couloir
routes.descent: Descend the southeast slopes of the peak, then follow the use trail and cross-country route back toward Upper Lamarck Lake.

routes.name: Petra
routes.descent: From the top, either walk off or rappel. For the walk-off, go left (south and southeast) over third and fourth class ground to the high point of the ridge, then trend down and left along ledges to easier ground. routes.name: East Slope
routes.desc: Follow the Meysan Lake trail, then climb talus to a chute that leads to the plateau and summit. Snow or ice can choke the chute well into summer.

routes.name: Lola Trail
routes.desc: A well-defined trail climbs through forest and Cold Stream Meadow toward the south ridge and summit. Easy and non-technical.

routes.name: East Slopes from Meysan Lake
routes.desc: Hike the Meysan Lakes trail to the lake, then climb the loose gully near the south side of the east ridge to the plateau and the summit blocks. Scree and talus all the way.

routes.name: Via Arc Pass
routes.desc: Reach Arc Pass, then climb scree and talus to the south summit. Downclimb a class 3 step into the notch, go up a short way and follow a ramp left onto easy scrambling to the highest point. Exposed; a rope may be welcome.

routes.name: North Face
routes.descent: The route ends on the summit plateau, crossed to the summit. The normal way off is the East Couloir route, passing Mills Lake to Ruby Lake where the trail back to the trailhead is picked up. Parties camped in the Fourth Recess can instead go back down the north face.

routes.name: Southwest Slope
routes.desc: The easy side is the southwest slope above the Crabtree Lakes. A common long approach crosses Discovery Pass and Crabtree Pass; the ridge from Crabtree Pass is slower and reaches class 3.

routes.name: West Slope
routes.desc: A straightforward class 2 line starts just south of the summit and angles up the west face to a broad gully.

routes.name: East Ridge from Armstrong Canyon
routes.desc: Climb the loose talus chute out of Armstrong Canyon to the crest, cross the high basin, and follow the talus of the east ridge to the summit. Water is scarce and the chute is loose.

routes.name: South Slope
routes.desc: Hike over Kearsarge Pass to the Bullfrog Lake area, then climb the loose scree and talus slopes to the summit ridge. The last few hundred feet are steeper, with a few easy moves on dark rock near the top.

routes.name: East Ridge
routes.desc: Hike over Taboose Pass and cross the Kings River, then go cross-country to the base of the east ridge. Climb the blocky toe and scramble the ridge, which has exposed class 3 with a move or two harder.

routes.name: Via Sallie Keyes Lakes
routes.desc: Hike the trail around Florence Lake and across the San Joaquin, take the cutoff use trail toward Selden Pass, and climb to Sallie Keyes Lakes. Continue over boulders and a bench below the summit; the final slopes are easier than they look.

routes.name: South Slope from Silliman Lake
routes.desc: Follow the Twin Lakes trail to Silliman Creek, go up the creek to Silliman Meadow and the friction slabs to Silliman Lake. Continue to the upper lake and climb the south slope to the summit.

routes.name: West Face of Mount Starr King
Antichrist Dihedral
routes.descent: From the top-out, scramble fourth class west into the gap that separates the main wall from Dawn Pillar and rappel into it (slung block and a single-bolt anchor), then scramble out the far side and hike third class down to a prominent gully. routes.name: South Slope from Red Lake
routes.desc: Hike the trail to Red Lake, then go up the bowl south of the peak on boulders and talus to the summit. Early season can bring a steep snow chute in the upper bowl.

routes.name: Standard route
routes.desc: Class 2 to the summit block, which is Class 4.

routes.name: Warren Canyon
routes.desc: Follow the creek trail up Warren Canyon, then easy talus to the plateau and a short ridge to the top.

routes.name: Northeast Face
routes.descent: head south along summit ridge, drop a short class 3 headwall to the east ridge, follow it down

routes.name: South Face
routes.descent: This is the standard route on the peak and also the way down: downclimb the same line from the summit block.

routes.name: Standard route
routes.desc: Class 4 to the summit block, which is Class 5.

routes.name: South West Ridge (aka Yellow Brick Road)
Goode Earth
routes.descent: The buttress tops out on the ridge below the summit. A second-class scramble along the east ridge reaches the summit if wanted. Descend the southeast slopes, second class, back to the Bishop Pass trail near Saddlerock Lake.

routes.name: Jonny B. Goode
routes.descent: Parties come down by rappelling the line, or by climbing up and right to third class terrain.

routes.name: The Goode Life
routes.descent: The route ends on the ridge top. Descend the peak's usual way: down and southeast over blocky ground to sandy slopes, then contour east between Saddlerock Lake and Bishop Lake to meet the Bishop Pass trail to the east.

routes.name: The Goode, the Grateful, and the Ganja!
West Ridge
routes.descent: After the traverse to the summit of Goode, descend the standard second-class route to the Bishop Pass trail at Saddlerock Lake.

routes.name: North Couloir Direct
routes.descent: From the col at the top of the couloir, a class 4 chute leads up and right to the summit. To get down, either reverse the route or downclimb the East Arete, which suits day trips.

routes.name: Stone Meysan
routes.descent: The route finishes with a blocky ridge of third to low fifth class that ends on the Irvine-Mallory divide. Hike south along the divide, then drop to Meysan Lake by the east slopes of Green Pass.

routes.name: Standard Route - south slopes
routes.descent: Come down the way you went up. Drop the scree and sand of the south slopes to the pass and return to Horseshoe Meadows by New Army Pass, or by Old Army Pass, whose trail drops past Cottonwood Lake 4. The route is a walk-up with no rope work, but snow in spring can call for an axe.

routes.name: East Arete via South East Ridge
Caught Inside
routes.descent: The route finishes at the east ridge, on the northeast shoulder, with an easy snow gully leading about 800 feet on to the summit. One option is to go on to the summit and walk down the east slopes. The other is to cut south over a rock buttress, which has no technical difficulty, and then drop onto the east slope. Do not drop into the prominent gully right under the finish, because it ends in clif

routes.name: Cowardice
routes.descent: The route ends on the Northwest Ridge. Either follow the ridge to the summit and descend the east face, or skip the summit: go down the ridge over loose third-class ground to a large open couloir on the north (skier's right) side, then descend very loose talus or snow.

routes.name: Deception
routes.descent: The route ends on the Northwest Ridge. Either follow the ridge to the summit and descend the east face, or skip the summit: go down the ridge over loose third-class ground to a large open couloir on the north (skier's right) side, then descend very loose talus or snow.

routes.name: Learning to Walk
routes.descent: The route joins the Northwest Ridge. Either follow the ridge to the summit and descend the east face, or skip the summit: go down the ridge over loose third-class ground to a large open couloir on the north (skier's right) side, then descend very loose talus or snow.

routes.name: Northwest Couloir
routes.descent: Walk off down the east slopes of the peak. Do not go back down the couloir itself, because rockfall there is serious.

routes.name: Psychopomp
routes.descent: The climbing ends on a ridge on the northeast shoulder, with easy snow leading about 800 feet on to the summit. One option is to go on to the summit and walk down the east slopes. The other is to cut south over a rock buttress, which has no technical difficulty, and then drop onto the east slope. Do not drop into the prominent gully right under the finish, because it ends in cliffs.

routes.name: From Trail by W + N ridge
Bloody Corner
routes.descent: Routes finish at the west summit. For the South Gully, which suits parties camped at Iceberg Lake, scramble east along the ridge toward the east summit, then find the third-class ramp dropping into the gully just before it. routes.descent: The roped climbing ends atop the pillar. Scramble or simul-climb a few hundred feet to the summit, joining the Mithril Dihedral ground. routes.name: East Arete
routes.descent: Descend the way you climbed: back along the East Ridge, with exposed but solid third class near the summits, to the Russell-Carillon pass, then easy scree down to Upper Boy Scout Lake. From the west summit you can alternatively use the South Gully, via a third-class ramp just before the east summit, if camped at Iceberg Lake; it is loose but quick.

routes.name: Fishhook Arête
routes.descent: The arete ends on the summit. Traverse toward the east summit and drop down a short third-class gully (the South Gully), then follow talus back to the base of the route and the trail to the col. Parties camped at Upper Boy Scout Lake can instead go over the east summit and take the exposed third-class East Ridge to the Russell-Carillon pass, then easy scree to the lake.

routes.name: Mithril Dihedral
routes.descent: Routes finish at the west summit. routes.name: Goldbug
routes.descent: The roped climbing ends on a large terrace where the west face stops being steep. Unrope and scramble fourth and easy fifth class, generally rightward, to the summit. routes.name: Avalanche Gulch
routes.descent: Descend the same route. When the snow is soft enough, many climbers glissade long sections of the gulch, but always take crampons off first and keep the ice axe ready to brake. In poor visibility it is easy to drift east off the route into Mud Creek Canyon, so navigate carefully on the way down.

routes.name: Hotlum-Wintun Ridge
routes.descent: Descend the line you climbed. From the summit, angle down the steep upper chute and onto the Wintun side, where the slope is steepest and a fall can slide a long way, so keep the axe in hand and do not glissade carelessly. routes.name: Swiss Arete
routes.descent: northwest ridge toward the neighbour peak, over to the north side at a spike, down a steep pitch and across a ledge to the notch, then the snowfield to the notch below

routes.name: East Buttress
routes.descent: The route finishes on the summit plateau, after merging with the East Face line near the top. Descend by the Mountaineers Route to the north: from the summit, walk west across the plateau to where the route topped out, and note the spot, since the rim all looks alike from above. routes.name: Hairline
routes.descent: Hairline meets the regular East Face line just above its ninth pitch, then three more pitches and some fourth class lead to the summit area.
