routes.name: Happy Cowboy (Whitney Edge Traverse)
routes.descent: The traverse ends on the summit. Walk the John Muir Trail south to where it joins the Whitney Trail, continue to Trail Crest, then follow the Whitney Trail east, a long way down, to Whitney Portal. A permit for the Whitney Zone is needed year-round, so carry it for the descent as well.

routes.name: Left Wing Extremist
routes.descent: The route finishes by joining the regular East Face line to the summit plateau. Descend the Mountaineers Route back to Iceberg Lake: from the summit, walk west across the plateau to where the route topped out, and note the spot, since the rim all looks alike from above. Steep, exposed third-class steps and ledges lead to the notch, then a long loose gully runs east to Iceberg Lake; some fourth-cla

routes.name: Direct East Face
routes.descent: The line merges with the regular East Face route where the Fresh Air Traverse begins, and finishes up that route to the summit plateau. Descend the Mountaineers Route back to Iceberg Lake: from the summit, walk west across the plateau to where the route topped out, and note the spot, since the rim all looks alike from above. Steep, exposed third-class steps and ledges lead to the notch, then a lon

routes.name: Our Own Devices
routes.descent: Two ways down. One is to rappel from a slung block into the gully of the Mountaineers Route and follow that route down to Iceberg Lake. The other is to go on to the summit of the first tower and walk off, which is easy climbing but a little run out and links well with the East Face or East Buttress. The Mountaineers Route is loose, so wear a helmet and avoid knocking rock onto parties below.

routes.name: The Great Book
routes.descent: Descend the Mountaineers Route from the summit plateau, back to Iceberg Lake: from the summit, walk west across the plateau to where the route topped out, and note the spot, since the rim all looks alike from above. Steep, exposed third-class steps and ledges lead to the notch, then a long loose gully runs east to Iceberg Lake; some fourth-class downclimbing is possible near the top. Early in the

routes.name: Hairline Free
routes.descent: Hairline meets the regular East Face line just above its ninth pitch, then three more pitches and some fourth class lead to the summit area. Descend the Mountaineers Route back to camp at Iceberg Lake: from the summit, walk west across the plateau to where the route topped out, and note the spot, since the rim all looks alike from above. Steep, exposed third-class steps and ledges lead to the notc

routes.name: Mount Whitney Trail, The
routes.descent: Retrace the trail from the summit: follow it south to Trail Crest, then drop east past Trail Camp, Consultation Lake, Outpost Camp and Lone Pine Lake to Whitney Portal, over six thousand feet below the summit. The trail is usually clear of snow from midsummer to early autumn. In spring and early summer, snow and ice linger on the upper switchbacks, and an axe and crampons are needed for the descen

routes.name: North Face
routes.descent: The route ends at the summit. Descend the Mountaineers Route back to Iceberg Lake: from the summit, walk west across the plateau to where the route topped out, and note the spot, since the rim all looks alike from above. Steep, exposed third-class steps and ledges lead to the notch, then a long loose gully runs east to Iceberg Lake; some fourth-class downclimbing is possible near the top. Early in

routes.name: SouthWest Edge
routes.descent: Finish on the flat summit area, then walk down the Whitney Trail, which is marked by cairns, past the saddle where the route began. The trail leads south to Trail Crest and then east down to Whitney Portal. Keep to the trail rather than the rim, because the wall below the summit area drops hundreds of feet and the rock near its edge is fractured.

routes.name: SouthWest Ridge
routes.descent: The scramble ends on the flat summit area. Walk down the Whitney Trail, marked by cairns, back past the notch where the scramble started; the trail leads south to Trail Crest and then east down to Whitney Portal.

routes.name: The Mountaineer's Route
routes.descent: Descend the Mountaineers Route. From the summit, walk west across the plateau to where the route topped out, and note the spot, since the rim all looks alike from above. Steep, exposed third-class steps and ledges lead to the notch, then a long loose gully runs east to Iceberg Lake; some fourth-class downclimbing is possible near the top. Early in the season, or after storms, snow and ice can stay

routes.name: Silver Linings Arete
routes.descent: From the summit, descend the east arete (third class), dropping to the second chute on that side and following it down, then traverse to Winchell Col without losing elevation. West of the col, take the left of the two forks and downclimb a loose gully at third to fourth class. A rappel station on the left side of the gully serves the drop-off partway down, and easier ground lies below it. The chut

routes.name: Training Day
routes.descent: The route continues up the south ridge to the summit. From the summit, descend the east arete (third class), dropping to the second chute on that side and following it down, then traverse to Winchell Col without losing elevation. West of the col, take the left of the two forks and downclimb a loose gully at third to fourth class. A rappel station on the left side of the gully serves the drop-off p

routes.name: Via Mulkey Pass
routes.desc: From Horseshoe Meadow climb to Mulkey Pass, then follow the crest trail south and leave it for a cross-country climb through foxtail pines and talus to the summit rocks. About 12 miles round trip with roughly 2,900 ft of gain.

routes.name: Standard route
routes.desc: Class 2 to the summit block, which is Class 3.

routes.name: Firebird Ridge
routes.descent: the easier class 3-4 line on the same ridge, climbed in 1922, is the popular way down

routes.name: West Ridge of North Guard-The parapet ridge
Saddle Route from Long Meadow
routes.desc: Hike in to Long Meadow, leave the trail at an old metal sign and cross the Middle Fork Tule River. Stay just north of the ridge and cut over to the saddle next to point 10,113, then go straight to the summit, avoiding brush.

routes.name: North Face North Couloir (right couloir)
routes.descent: The ice ends at a notch. From there a low fifth-class scramble to climbers' right reaches the summit, or you can descend south toward Conness Lake.

routes.name: Via Olancha Pass and the PCT
routes.desc: Climb to Olancha Pass, follow the Pacific Crest Trail north along the west side of the crest, then leave it for the summit. The last stretch is sand, then big granite blocks.

routes.name: Indian Wells Canyon
routes.desc: Follow the old road to a wilderness barricade, then a canyon trail to a clearing near 6,100 ft. Take the right fork on a use trail through dark boulders and finish up slabs; about 7 miles round trip with 3,200 ft of gain.

routes.name: Northwest Ridge
routes.desc: Take the South Fork Big Pine Creek trail to Elinore Lake, climb to the crest at the notch, and follow the ridge to the high pinnacle. A steep class 4 ramp is the key obstacle.

routes.name: East Ridge from Piute Pass
routes.desc: Hike over Piute Pass, cross Humphreys Basin to the saddle on the east ridge, then scramble boulders to the summit.

routes.name: Northeast Ridge
routes.desc: A very long trip from Twin Lakes through Kerrick Canyon to Seavey Pass, then up the northeast ridge to a saddle. Drop to a north-side cirque and take a talus chute to the north ridge.

routes.name: Rocky Canyon
routes.desc: Follow the Rocky Canyon use trail to the broad area below the south ridge, then climb the ridge to the summit. The trail can be hard to follow where snow lingers.

routes.name: West Face
routes.desc: Reach the cirque of lakes between Black and Red Kaweah from Big Arroyo, then climb the broad west face on loose talus and boulders, keeping well right of Black Kaweah's face. The crest is gained just below the summit; the rock is very unstable. Class 2 to the summit block, which is Class 3.

routes.name: North Couloir
routes.descent: Head northwest over scree slopes to a saddle, then go north back down to Lake Wit-So-Nah-Pah.

routes.name: North Ridge Direct
routes.descent: The route finishes on the summit of Royce Peak, after a long stretch of third and fourth class and easy fifth class along the ridge. A walk-off to the south leads down from there.

routes.name: San Joaquin Ridge
routes.desc: Follow the jeep road and use trail north along San Joaquin Ridge, with easy navigation and little elevation gain.

routes.name: Northwest Slope
routes.desc: A non-technical class 2 ascent from the northwest; long approach via Lamarck Col, the John Muir Trail and Ionian Basin.

routes.name: Lookout Trail
routes.desc: A steady trail climbs about 1,500 ft in 2.5 miles, crossing the Pacific Crest Trail. It ends with a long metal staircase up to the lookout.

routes.name: Albanita Trail and Northeast Ridge
routes.desc: Follow an old road onto the Albanita Trail to a saddle on the northeast ridge, then go cross-country past a granite crag to the rocky summit. About 3.3 miles round trip with 1,100 ft of gain and a short exposed scramble at the end.

routes.name: South Slope via Longley Pass
routes.desc: Climb the sandy scree to Longley Pass from the Cedar Grove side, then take class 3 rock to the summit, which sits on the west side of the ridge.

routes.name: North Ridge
routes.desc: Hike the trail past Statham Meadow to the saddle near the Geraldine Lakes, then walk the easy ridge to the summit. The trail is faint in places.

routes.name: North Ridge
routes.desc: Reach the Pacific Crest Trail saddle north of the summit, then climb the north ridge. Expect loose rock, side-hilling and tricky chute-finding on exposed third class.

routes.name: Southeast Face from St. Marys Pass
routes.desc: Take the trail to St. Marys Pass, then north along the broad ridge until the trail fades at the saddle before the peak. Climb the south face of dirt, sand and scree, with some class 2 rock near the top.

routes.name: Southeast Face Ramp
routes.desc: Cross Shepherd Pass, drop to the Kern, and climb Milestone Basin to the base of the southeast face. A prominent ramp leads up the left side to a keyhole and the summit plateau, with the high point at its north end.

routes.name: West Ridge
routes.desc: Take the Big Meadow Trail to the saddle at the head of Taylor Creek, follow the ridge to the base of the dome, and finish up a short chimney from the saddle. Class 2 to the summit block, which is Class 3.

routes.name: Barefoot Bynum
routes.descent: traverse down and right into north couloir from top of lower buttress

routes.name: Dark Star
routes.descent: From the top of the crag, work down the gully for a long way, staying high and heading straight down before it steepens sharply and drops to the right. Ledges and steps lead to an obvious rappel off blocks at the very top of Contact Pass. A different gully has anchors but lands well below the pass, so you climb sand back up to it. At the pass itself, expect loose blocks, sand and difficult route f

routes.name: Moon Goddess Arete
routes.descent: The route ends on the back slopes of Temple Crag, and the summit is a short hike from the top if time allows. The way down is the standard Contact Pass descent: follow the back slopes to steep rock where a short rappel off fixed slings reaches Contact Pass. Below the pass, snow or loose scree and talus lead back to the lakes. Early in the season the snow below the pass can be kicked down or glissa

routes.name: Sun Ribbon Arete
routes.descent: The usual way down is through Contact Pass, which is unpleasant however you reach it. Reach the pass and rappel once, on a single rope, from the station furthest right, which puts you on scree; then slog back down to the snowfield and your camp, or to the trail and the car. Start early, as the descent needs attention and the crag is exposed to electrical storms. A way to avoid the pass is to trave

routes.name: Temple, Galey, Sill Traverse
routes.descent: The traverse ends on Mount Sill. From its summit, descend the third-class ridge in the direction of Polemonium, then drop into the L-shaped couloir and Glacier Notch to reach the Palisade Glacier. The starts of both are not obvious, but cairns usually mark them. From the glacier, you can either go straight down to Second or Third Lake, which is more direct and best with snow, or follow the trail p

routes.name: Venusian Blind
routes.descent: From the top of the arete, descend east on a climbers' trail toward Contact Pass. The trail turns into class 3 above the pass and then steepens to class 4 and 5 terrain, where most parties rappel from slings to the pass. Below the pass, snow can be glissaded and rock and scree lead back to the lakes. A rappel station on the left side of the arete higher up allows a short rappel into the gully, fro

routes.name: Southeast Slope from Birch Lake
routes.desc: Follow the Birch Creek trail to Birch Lake, climb the steep ramp west of the lake to the crest, then ascend talus and snow to the summit. The ramp holds snow into summer and may need crampons.

routes.name: Boy Scout Falls
routes.descent: Walk off to climber's right, or rappel using V-threads or the anchors on the left side of the flow. Two ropes are needed unless you walk off.

routes.name: Thunder Col and East Ridge
routes.desc: Go up the Bubbs Creek and East Lake drainages past Lake Reflection to the lakes below Thunder Col, then climb the east ridge or southeast slopes. The summit crux is a short exposed move on the north summit block. Class 3 to the summit block, which is Class 4.

routes.name: Underhill Couloir
routes.descent: reverse the route, or descend Southwest Chute Number 1

routes.name: Via the Pacific Crest Trail
routes.desc: Reach the Pacific Crest Trail and follow it to the saddle just southeast of the peak, then walk a short distance to the summit. A longer, easier approach comes along the crest trail from Donner Pass.

routes.name: East Ridge via Dykeman Pass
routes.desc: Take the Blue Canyon Trail to its north end, continue up to Dykeman Pass, drop into the Alpine Creek drainage and climb talus to the east ridge. The ridge has some class 3 scrambling.

routes.name: South Slope from Tulainyo Lake
routes.desc: Climb the Mountaineers Route to the Russell-Carillon plateau, cross the Russell-Carillon pass (class 3 on the north side) to Tulainyo Lake, then walk the sandy south slopes to the summit.

routes.name: Northwest Shoulder
routes.descent: Descend to University Pass, then go down to Robinson Lake.

routes.name: South Slope from Farewell Gap
routes.desc: Hike to Farewell Gap, then climb the talus slope on the west side of the gap to the summit. Easy class 2 and commonly done as a day trip.

routes.name: Golden Pillar
routes.descent: The route ends on a sandy slope above the last block, from which careful fifth-class scrambling leads to the middle summit of Whorl Mountain. Descend by the third-class southeast face route, the gully just left of the pillar.

routes.name: North Ridge
routes.descent: The last pitch finishes directly on the summit. Descend by the popular class 3-4 southeast chute, the southeast face route.

routes.name: East Ramp
routes.desc: Backpack to the Vestal Creek camp, then climb the long slabby ramp on the east face; the upper couloir is steeper, closer to Class 4. Ice axe useful in early season.

routes.name: North Ridge
routes.desc: Trail up McCullough Gulch then a talus ridge; parking is restricted at this trailhead.

routes.name: Gash Couloir
routes.descent: The couloir tops out on Gash Ridge, which can be followed to the summit. Options from there include downclimbing the angling snow couloir to the right of Ormes Buttress, or going over Ellingwood Point and down ledges; the route itself can be rappelled but the rock is rotten and rockfall is frequent. A steep, snowy ridge can be downclimbed to a snowfield and then the basin below the face.

routes.name: Rocky Mountain Hypergoulotte
routes.descent: One way down is to rappel off the ridge back onto the snow ramp, downclimb the ramp to the fixed pin and rappel from it onto steep alpine ice, which can be downclimbed or rappelled to the ramp. Next, move right along the ramp to a point beneath Ellingwood and glissade down into the bowl under the face.

routes.name: South Ridge
routes.desc: Long grassy and talus ridge in the Sangre de Cristo Range accessed from the Lily Lake road.

routes.name: North Ridge
routes.desc: Rocky ridge scramble that is usually combined with French Mountain and Frasco Benchmark.

routes.name: Northeast Ridge
routes.descent: reverse the ascent, or descend the peak's northwest crest to its col with Conundrum Peak; with good snow a long glissade runs from that col

routes.name: South Ridge and Couloir
routes.desc: Trail to Cathedral Lake, then a loose gully and ridge scramble to the summit above Aspen; rockfall and late-season loose scree are the main concerns.

routes.name: South Slope
routes.desc: Gentle slopes above the Mosquito Range, usually done on its own or with neighboring McNamee and Traver.

routes.name: North Ridge
routes.desc: Long ridge hike at the southern end of the Sawatch, started from the Baldwin Creek area.

routes.name: Northeast Ridge
routes.desc: Talus ridge in the Tenmile Range; often joined with Pacific and Atlantic peaks.

routes.name: Southeast Slopes
routes.desc: Short climb from a high trailhead above Leadville.

routes.name: South/Southwest Ridge
routes.desc: Moderate hike from the Clohesy Lake area above Winfield with a talus finish.

routes.name: Southeast Ridge
routes.desc: Short tundra and talus climb from the Blue Lakes road, often paired with Drift Peak by a Class 3 traverse.

routes.name: Southeast Ridge
routes.desc: Grassy ridge and flank above the Halfmoon drainage; often linked in a day with Frasco Benchmark and Casco Peak.

routes.name: North Ridge
routes.desc: Reach the Rock of Ages saddle near 13,000 ft, then follow the ridge crest with loose rock and a Class 4 crux (Class 3 bypass exists). About 11.25 miles round trip with 4,100 ft of gain.

routes.name: Grizzly Couloir
routes.descent: The couloir tops out a short scramble from the summit and steepens as you climb, to around 45 to 50 degrees near the top. Either walk down the west slopes to the road, or glissade and downclimb the couloir with great care. Rocks fall from the cliffs on either side, so wear a helmet. A fall high up could slide a long way, though the angle eases a lot near the bottom. Check the avalanche forecast fi

routes.name: South Ridge (from Garfield Peak)
routes.desc: Follow the ridge over rock and talus with only informal use-trails, usually combined with Garfield Peak; about 10.8 miles round trip with 3,790 ft of gain. Third-class bits can be bypassed on the west side.

routes.name: Southface
routes.desc: Climb through steep gullies on the south face above Geneva Lake; snow can linger in the gullies.

routes.name: Northwest Ridge
routes.desc: Remote peak near the Continental Divide whose mileage depends on how far a high-clearance vehicle can drive; rough ridge scrambling near the top.

routes.name: Southwest Slopes
routes.desc: A trail from American Basin past Sloan Lake to the summit ridge; the shortest way up a San Juan fourteener.

routes.name: North Section from Half Moon Creek
routes.desc: Long trail and ridge walk near Holy Cross with a talus finish.

routes.name: East Slopes
routes.desc: Gentle walk-up on tundra slopes in the Mosquito Range; one of the easiest Centennial 13ers.

routes.name: South Slopes
routes.desc: Long ridge and talus ascent in the Sangre de Cristos; a side trip to the Iron Nipple is optional.

routes.name: Northeast Ridge
routes.desc: Rocky ridge scramble that is normally combined with North Apostle.

routes.name: Northeast Ridge
routes.desc: Straightforward ridge walk, normally strung together with American and Niagara peaks.

routes.name: Southwest Slopes
routes.desc: Remote Chicago Basin objective reached by train; the final slopes are loose.

routes.name: North-Northwest Ridge
routes.desc: Steep grass and talus ridge above Lake Creek near Twin Lakes.

routes.name: Keyhole Route
routes.descent: Reverse the ascent, or downclimb the north wall to the old cable line and rap

routes.name: West Ridge via Willow Creek
routes.desc: Long approach to a high basin followed by a ridge scramble with some Class 3 moves in the Sangre de Cristos.

routes.name: Northeast Slope
routes.desc: Short, easy tundra climb from Kite Lake; commonly done with the Decalibron group.

routes.name: Southwest Ridge
routes.desc: Tundra ridge off the Argentine Pass road near Georgetown with some rocky sections.

routes.name: East Ridge
routes.desc: Steady climb with considerable loose talus on the upper ridge, usually done with neighboring Quail Mountain.

routes.name: FUNdus
routes.descent: Bushwhack through the willows at the top to a conifer with slings and a rappel ring, and rappel from there.

routes.name: The Birth Canal
routes.descent: Rappel from the slung tree near the upper left end of the flow; the rope has to be long enough to reach the base.

routes.name: Mum's the Word
routes.descent: A walk-off exists leftward between the tiers. The belay for the lower tier is a tree near the upper tier.

routes.name: Southeast Slopes
routes.desc: Steady grassy and talus slopes above Halfmoon Creek.

routes.name: West Ridge
routes.desc: Short, mostly walking ascent along the Continental Divide ridge from the pass, with a bit of rocky stepping near the top.

routes.name: North Spur from Hoosier Pass
routes.desc: Broad spur above Hoosier Pass; a short hike with talus near the top.

routes.name: West Slopes
routes.desc: A trail from Guanella Pass across the willows and up the west slopes, with easy talus at the top.

routes.name: Coming of Age
routes.descent: The fourth pitch is low fifth-class ground to the ridge crest below the summit. To get off, walk to climber's right along obvious grassy ledges, with perhaps a fourth-class move or two.

routes.name: Another Load of Ginormous Excitement  (aka The Cichon Variation)
Miller's Face
routes.descent: After cleaning the anchor, scramble up the ledge in the direction of Rusty Dagger and follow it as a third-class walk-off to the gully, which is hiked back up to Summit Lake.

routes.name: Damn it Feels Good to be a Hamsta
Diamond Couloir
routes.descent: Follow the snow as it steepens up to the cliff band where it stops, then keep left (east) of the steep rock and take a couple of Class 4 steps up to the west ridge. Old tat marks where parties went right; avoid that. The summit is a short Class 2 ridge walk from there. In good snow cover the couloir is also skied back to Summit Lake. Crampons and an axe are the norm, and a rope is optional for the

routes.name: Concrete Shoes Won't Help Ya In Da River
routes.descent: The route finishes on the ridge above the buttress. Walk east along the ridge to the saddle and drop to the Mount Blue Sky road, then follow the road back down toward Echo Lake. The road is closed to vehicles in winter, and the walk down it is long, so budget daylight and be ready for snow-covered pavement.

routes.name: Double Dragon (right side)
routes.descent: The gully tops out on the hikers' trail that leads to Mt Spaulding; follow that trail back to the Chicago Lakes Overlook.

routes.name: Far Right Dihedral (2nd Apron)
routes.descent: The route ends on a large terrace; cross it to the left and exit by the easiest path to the ridge. To come down, drop into the couloir between the Second and Third Aprons: a short rappel from the top gets you onto steep snow that is then downclimbed. Alternatively walk down one of the main trails along the ridge. Bring crampons and an axe for the snow.

routes.name: Iration
routes.descent: The route finishes at the top of the buttress, at the trail. Follow the trail back along the rim toward the overlook and Summit Lake. Knife blades and small pins are the key gear, and the exit ground is easy mixed terrain.

routes.name: North Face Crag
routes.descent: Each of these lines ends on the ridge just west of the summit. From the top, walk back east along the ridge to the summit area and its parking, the way the easy approach comes in. Snow on the ridge can be corniced, so stay back from the north edge.

routes.name: Northwest Couloir
routes.descent: Leave the couloir by a Class 4 traverse, then walk the ridge a short way to the summit. Come down by the summit road back toward Summit Lake, which is closed to vehicles in winter. A rope is optional; some parties carry pickets or a light rack.

routes.name: Road Less Warren
routes.descent: Hike to the saddle on the ridge above and descend to the Mount Blue Sky road, then follow the road back toward Echo Lake. A fixed cord above the ice lets you lower into the drainage rather than downclimb. The road is closed to vehicles in winter, so expect a long walk out.

routes.name: Telepherique
routes.descent: The route ends on the ridge just west of the summit. Walk back east along the ridge to the summit parking area, retracing the easy approach. Cornices can form on the ridge edge, so stay back from it.

routes.name: The Bib (1st Apron)
routes.descent: From the third class ledge at the top, one rope-length rappel puts you on the scree and talus below. Alternatively, work up on rock to the ridge. Beware of loose rock on the talus.

routes.name: The Road
routes.descent: After the ice, scramble to the top of the buttress, then head up and left to a col on the ridgeline. Drop down the far side to the Mount Blue Sky road and follow the road back to Echo Lake. The road is closed to vehicles in winter, so the walk out is long.

routes.name: The Snave
routes.descent: The couloir finishes in the notch next to the summit, above the parking area. The easy way off is a second vehicle at the top; otherwise walk the road back down to Summit Lake, which is closed to vehicles in winter. Crampons and an axe are the standard kit.

routes.name: West Ridge
routes.desc: From Summit Lake over Mount Spalding and along the west ridge, with talus scrambling near the top.

routes.name: Seven Sins (Sinners on Sunday to High Variance)
Top Gun Couloir
routes.descent: Parties can glissade the Sunrise Couloir, keeping clear of the cornice that builds over its top, or walk down either Spalding Ridge or Evans Ridge. Spalding is typically the quicker of the two.

routes.name: The Loft Route
routes.desc: Follow the Longs Peak trail to Chasm Lake, climb the couloir south of the Ship's Prow and a ledge near 12,800 ft to the Loft, then boulder-hop to the summit block. About 11 miles round trip with 4,500 ft of gain.

routes.name: The Flying Buttress
routes.descent: scramble down the gully on the west side

routes.name: Northeast Ridge
routes.desc: Ridge walk usually combined with American and Jones peaks.

routes.name: Southwest Ridge
routes.desc: Tundra and talus ridge in the Collegiate Peaks, often combined with Ice Mountain.

routes.name: East Slopes
routes.desc: Follow the Mohawk Lakes trail, then a faint trail and off-trail terrain to a loose gully near 13,200 ft; hard Class 2 with rockfall. About 11 miles round trip with 3,650 ft of gain, less from the upper road.

routes.name: North Face Couloirs
routes.descent: Descend as for the peak itself, by the east ridge. Cornices overhang the west ridge above the route.

routes.name: South Ridge and Slopes
routes.desc: Remote tundra walk reached by a rough road near Creede; adds a few miles if the road is not driven.

routes.name: Northwest Couloir
routes.desc: Backpack up Ruby Creek to a camp in the northwest basin, then climb the large couloir and a stiff slope to third-class scrambling at the summit block. Often combined with Turret Peak.

routes.name: Don't Follow the Goats
routes.descent: Past the optional fifth-class final pitch, a few hundred feet of fourth and fifth class scrambling along ledges on the ridgeline reaches the top of the buttress. From there, exit by the Hero Traverse, or go below the southeast side of the Zeb's Arete ridgeline and up the fourth-class gully to the top.

routes.name: Zeb's Arete
routes.descent: The climbing ends on the summit plateau, and the car is a short walk back along the road across the rocks. Step on rock rather than on the fragile alpine plants.

routes.name: Anus Grape
routes.descent: The route joins the last pitch of Solar Winds to the north summit; an easier finish over moderate ground reaches the terrace below the south summit spire. That terrace is the top of the descent chimney, which goes down the west (back) side of the formation.

routes.name: Solar Winds
routes.descent: The route finishes on the north summit. Go down a short rappel or downclimb in the chimney at the north summit's south end to reach to the broad terrace under the south summit spire. That terrace is the top of the descent chimney, which goes down the west (back) side of the formation.

routes.name: Walk on the Wild Side
routes.descent: Rappel from slings at the boulders on top, pass south through the slot at the back of the main pinnacle, and finish with bolted rappels to the ground.

routes.name: The Grand Tour
routes.descent: Scramble up blocky ground toward the top, then traverse west (climber's right) across the head of the Total Abandon drainage; that section is loose and may deserve a rope. Alternatively, keep climbing to the highway and hike down the Upper Crags trail.

routes.name: Warren Route
routes.descent: From the top, continue up and then right on fourth-class ground to the clear path back to the road. Loose rock makes the last stretch across the gully awkward.

routes.name: Fairy Tale Direct
routes.descent: Go up and to the left, then follow the ridge that separates the Blue Run and Pigs ski lines back down.

routes.name: Goldy Locks
routes.descent: Continue upward and cross to the left until the gentle slopes of Blue Run can be walked down. Alternatively, walk off to the right after the first pitch, moving quickly under the old rockslide scar.

routes.name: Crack Thief
routes.descent: The route ends on a large ledge near the top of the shield. Either rappel west from just below the ledge, using the tat and rap ring there, or keep scrambling up the broken ground above the ledge and walk down Big Blue.

routes.name: Abruzzi Ridge
routes.descent: Walk off to the east by way of Big Blue.

routes.name: Big Blue
routes.descent: Because the toll road crosses the slope at the bottom and again at the top, a car shuttle is easy, and the slope is most often used by skiers and snowboarders. The upper end is on the road, so you can finish there. Check the avalanche forecast first.

routes.name: Center Couloir of Three Little Pigs (Flying W)
Chimney, The
routes.descent: Ski down, or walk down by way of the Big Blue slope to the east. The couloir can hide rocks that make a ski descent hazardous unless it is well filled in. Check the avalanche forecast first.

routes.name: Left Couloir of Three Little Pigs (Flying W)
Little Italy
routes.descent: Ski down, or walk down by way of the Big Blue slope to the east. Carry an axe and check the avalanche forecast first.

routes.name: Right Couloir of Three Little Pigs (Flying W)
Boss Hogg
routes.descent: Walk off the top, heading climber's right (west), and scramble down the class 4 approach ground back to the base. If a rope is left fixed in the chimney, keep it coiled so it cannot fall into the chimney, which snags ropes.

routes.name: Der Kinder
routes.descent: Finish up Excitable Boy or Keelhauled, or rappel the line.

routes.name: Excitable Boy
routes.descent: Rappel down the line into the gully on the right of the routes. A continuing line up dihedrals reaches the summit of the slab, but that finish means walking all the way around to get back to packs.

routes.name: Keelhauled
routes.descent: Rappel from the shared belay anchor, the one used for Excitable Boy.

routes.name: 66 Years of Fun
routes.descent: The third pitch finishes on a ledge even with where Total Abandon ends. A simple scramble reaches the walk-off ledge that Total Abandon parties use, and from there you return to the road and car.

routes.name: Blind Assumption
routes.descent: The chimney finishes toward the summit snowfields. Most parties break sharply right near the top, cross over the top of Total Abandon and follow the ridge back toward the car. Rappelling the route is also done.

routes.name: Blind Luck
routes.descent: After the last short pitch the technical difficulty ends. Walk off to the right across the tops of Blind Assumption and Total Abandon and continue to the highway. Rappelling Blind Assumption is the alternative.

routes.name: Bottomless Dogleg
routes.descent: The couloir exits at the lip near the road, southeast of Little Pike's Peak, so the walk back to the car is short.

routes.name: Furloughed
routes.descent: After the final pitch, easy snow and turf lead to the top. Climb a little higher and leave by the exit Total Abandon uses, which returns you to the road.

routes.name: Guide's Couloir
routes.descent: Climb the remaining easy snow toward the summit and stop at the shoulder just short of it, where the hikers' trail leads down.

routes.name: Three Dragons
routes.descent: The last pitch is broken ground to the top of the Corinthian Column. From there the usual walk-off is to scramble up the buttress and head off to the right toward the highway.

routes.name: Total Abandon
routes.descent: The gully above the technical climbing leads on toward the summit area, but most parties bail off to the right across the top of the Corinthian Column and walk back to the road and car. Spring avalanche danger on this face is real, so check the forecast before committing.

routes.name: Zeb's Big Butt Couloir
routes.descent: The couloir ends at a platform near the start of the Hero Traverse, which leads back to the toll road and the car. The traverse faces east and warms early, so factor that into the timing.

routes.name: Tava Ridge
routes.descent: The way out climbs rather than descends: work right along a ledge and gully, taking the ledge's easy scrambling to dodge the worst of the gully. It ends on a patch of tundra and talus, from which you walk to the trail and road and follow the road back to the pullout.

routes.name: Butterfingers
routes.descent: Top out the formation, then walk south along the summit crest toward the road, keeping to the west side until grassy ledges let you step down into the drainage again. Some routes on the formation have a non-permanent rappel line.

routes.name: The Ole  6
routes.descent: The roof traverse ends on or just below the top of the buttress. Either rappel Blind Assumption, or scramble up the buttress and walk off to the right toward the highway.

routes.name: Katana Ridge
routes.descent: Rappelling is the preferred way down, rather than hiking the Dinosaur Couloir, because it does less damage to the ground and the wildlife. The rappel anchors are behind the top-out. Tie knots in the rope ends, since the line may be longer than one rope reaches, then scramble down the gully to the base of the wall.

routes.name: Toga Party
routes.descent: After a mossy top-out, scramble up a short way, then cross right over the top of Total Abandon to return to the road and car.

routes.name: Northeast Ridge
routes.descent: Descend the same route, reversing the ledges, gullies, green wall and ridge gap back to the saddle, then down the steep scree slope to the amphitheater. Go slowly: the loose terrain is more dangerous going down, and the cairned line is easy to miss from above.

routes.name: Goat Urea
routes.descent: Scramble off to the west from the rock outcrops at the top of the second pitch, then work west and pick a gully that goes down.

routes.name: Blue Gold
routes.descent: Walk off to the left and go down the couloir. Some seasons leave a short ice step in the couloir, which is bypassed with a V-thread rappel back to the base.

routes.name: Claim Jumper
routes.descent: Traverse east from the top and walk down the prominent boxed couloir. Avalanche conditions in that couloir deserve attention, so check the forecast.

routes.name: Noxious Fumes
routes.descent: Descend the standard east ridge.

routes.name: Sluice Box
routes.descent: Descend the east ridge or the Quandary Couloir.

routes.name: The Canary Couloir
routes.descent: The east ridge is the top-out, and the standard east ridge route leads back down. A third-class escape gully on climber's left about halfway up may reach the east ridge sooner.

routes.name: Goldschlager
routes.descent: Rappel the route or downclimb.

routes.name: North Star
routes.descent: Scramble off to the west, or rappel the route.

routes.name: Ursa Major
routes.descent: From the upper pitches you can walk off west down scree and talus. Otherwise rappel from the fixed anchor near the top of the fifth pitch to the ledge anchor, then straight down to the bolted anchor of a summer sport route, which reaches the ground.

routes.name: Yukon Jack
routes.descent: Walk off the top of the second pitch back down to the first pitch belay, then rappel to the base.

routes.name: Bourbon Beaver
routes.descent: Walk off to the right down talus and scree.

routes.name: East Ridge
routes.desc: A trail up the broad east ridge from the Blue Lakes road; one of the most-climbed fourteeners.

routes.name: Second Reincarnation of the Golden Goat
North Ridge (from Culebra Peak)
routes.desc: Reached only across private ranch land with a permit; it is a ridge walk usually done after Culebra Peak.

routes.name: East Slope/Ridge
routes.desc: Very long Weminuche Wilderness hike, usually made an overnight, over gentle grassy terrain.

routes.name: East Ridge
routes.desc: Long grassy ridge in the remote eastern San Juans; mileage depends heavily on how far a vehicle can drive up the Stewart Creek road.

routes.name: West Face (White Couloir)
routes.desc: Steep couloir and west-face scrambling reached from the Maroon Lake area; very loose rock makes rockfall a serious hazard, so helmets and small parties matter.

routes.name: Dead Dog Couloir
routes.descent: The upper couloir averages about 45 degrees and ends some 150 to 200 feet under the summit, so scramble the rest of the way up. Descend the south ridge to the low saddle between Torreys and Grays, then glissade or downclimb into the basin, or follow the trail down from the saddle. Stones come off the upper walls once the sun warms them, so wear a helmet. Carry an axe and crampons. Check the avalan

routes.name: South Paw Couloir
routes.descent: The gully meets the ridge south of Torreys' summit, close to the trail linking Grays and Torreys. Descend by reversing the route, or climb the last 350 feet to the summit and take the Kelso Ridge down, or head south to the saddle and take the trail down, or go up to Grays Peak and walk down its trail. A standing wave or small serac near the top can be passed on the left or lower, depending on cond

routes.name: West Ridge
routes.desc: Remote Grenadier peak reached from Vestal Basin with exposed ridge climbing.

routes.name: Northwest Slope
routes.desc: Talus slope above Chicago Basin, normally combined with Pigeon Peak.

routes.name: Southwest Ridge
routes.desc: Remote ridge hike from the Silver Creek road near Redcloud.

routes.name: West Ridge
routes.desc: Tundra ridge reached by a rough 4x4 road near Redcloud; also climbed in a combo with its neighbor.

routes.name: Southeast Ridge
routes.desc: Open ridge and loose talus above Telluride's Ophir area with a short final scramble.

routes.name: South Face
routes.desc: Backpack the Colorado Trail and Elk Creek to Vestal Creek camp, then contour below the cliffs from the Arrow-Vestal saddle to a couloir on the southeast face. Mostly Class 2+ rock; ice axe useful early in the season.

routes.name: Southwest Ridge
routes.descent: Descend the way you came: reverse the ridge, including the climb back up out of the notch to the false summit, then retrace the Class 3 ledges to the Wilson Peak–Gladstone saddle, cross back to the Rock of Ages saddle, and follow the trail down to the trailhead.

routes.name: Mount Rose Trail
routes.desc: A well-defined trail from the highway pass climbs about 2,000 feet over roughly five miles to a saddle and the summit.

routes.name: Van Hoevenberg and MacIntyre Range Trails
routes.desc: Follow the blue-blazed Van Hoevenberg Trail about a mile to the yellow-blazed MacIntyre Range Trail, then climb about 3.3 miles to the summit. The upper trail grows steeper and rockier, with about 2,900 ft of total gain.

routes.name: Allen Brook herd path
routes.desc: Long, muddy day; the Opalescent River bridge is gone so the crossing can be hazardous at high water. Path: Hanging Spear Falls (East River) Trail to Allen Brook herd path. Starts at Upper Works / Tahawus Road.

routes.name: Great Range Trail from the Lake Road
routes.desc: Ladders beside Beaver Meadow Falls and steep sections; crossing the reserve on foot needs a reservation in the warm season. Path: Gothics access trail and Great Range Trail via Beaver Meadow Falls.

routes.name: Shorey's Shortcut
routes.desc: Long day with ladders and rock slabs; the exposed summit is often combined with Haystack or Saddleback. Path: Phelps Trail and Shorey's Shortcut. Starts at The Garden, Keene Valley.

routes.name: The Brothers Trail
routes.desc: Climb over the three Brothers for 3.2 miles to a junction, then continue to the summit at 3.4 miles. About 6.8 miles round trip with roughly 2,950 ft of gain.

routes.name: Via Mount Colvin
routes.desc: Reached over Colvin on the practical route; the Elk Lake approach is far longer. Path: Gill Brook Trail over Colvin, then path to Blake.

routes.name: Cascade Mountain Trail
routes.desc: About 2.4 miles one way; at the junction near mile 2, go left for the final stretch of bare rock marked by yellow blazes and cairns. The trailhead lot fills early.

routes.name: Uphill Brook herd path
routes.desc: Herd path leaves near the Uphill lean-to and climbs a steep, slippery cliff band; the first high point is a false summit. Path: Calamity Brook Trail to unmarked herd path. Starts at Upper Works, Newcomb.

routes.name: Via Santanoni ridge
routes.desc: Reached along the ridge beyond Santanoni; the boggy col below it is notoriously wet. Path: Santanoni Express herd path and ridge from Upper Works. Starts at Upper Works, Newcomb.

routes.name: Via Bear Den
routes.desc: Long push along the summit ridge; snow spikes advised on steeper parts of the Elk Pass side in winter. Path: Lake Road to Dial via Bear Den.

routes.name: Beckhorn Trail from Elk Lake
routes.desc: About 6.6 miles one way with roughly 3,700 ft of gain. The upper Beckhorn is steep, eroded and exposed on slab, and the longer Hunters Pass Trail is a gentler alternative.

routes.name: Seward Range herd path
routes.desc: Summit sits just off the ridge path beyond Seward; normally done as part of the range. Path: Blueberry Trail and Seward Range herd path. Starts at Corey's Road parking area.

routes.name: Herd path from Marble Mountain
routes.desc: Cairn-marked junction past Marble Mountain leads to an unofficial herd path; the summit has a false top before the plaque. Path: Marble Mountain route from the Atmospheric Science Research Center road. Starts at Atmospheric Science Research Center road, Wilmington.

routes.name: East Face Cirque - Several Routes for the Explorer
Ridge Trail
routes.desc: About 5.4 miles round trip with roughly 3,050 ft of gain, the shortest of the main routes. The Roaring Brook Trail (6.6 miles round trip) is the other common option.

routes.name: Beaver Meadow Falls Trail to the Range Trail
routes.desc: Walk Lake Road about 2 miles, then take the Gothics trail past Beaver Meadow Falls, with ladders on the steep section to the Range Trail. Turn left along the ridge to the summit; about 11.4 miles round trip.

routes.name: Dix Range herd path
routes.desc: Formerly East Dix; pointed rock summit reached by unmarked path east of South Dix. Path: Dix Range crest herd path from Elk Lake. Starts at Elk Lake trailhead.

routes.name: Via Lake Tear of the Clouds
routes.desc: Marked trail to Lake Tear of the Clouds, then a faint herd path to the summit. Path: Marcy Dam and Lake Arnold/Feldspar trails to Lake Tear, then herd path. Starts at Adirondak Loj / High Peaks Information Center.

routes.name: Dix Range herd path
routes.desc: Unmarked herd path along the Dix crest, with tight brush and rock scrambles; usually done with Dix. Path: Dix Range crest herd path from Elk Lake. Starts at Elk Lake trailhead.

routes.name: Via Algonquin Peak
routes.desc: Done as an out-and-back over Algonquin, with a steep unmarked final stretch. Path: Algonquin Peak trail, then herd path to Iroquois. Starts at Adirondak Loj / High Peaks Information Center.

routes.name: Wedge Brook and Range Trail from St. Huberts
routes.desc: About 8.8 miles round trip with roughly 3,000 ft of gain via West River, Wedge Brook and the State Range Trail. The Garden trailhead via the Phelps and Range trails is the other common approach.

routes.name: Macomb Slide
routes.desc: Slide is steep and loose; the first 2.3 miles from Elk Lake cross private land and the trail closes during big game season. Path: Hunters Pass Trail to Slide Brook, then slide and herd path. Starts at Elk Lake trailhead.

routes.name: Gill Brook Trail
routes.desc: Steep slab and a challenging spot near the summit; usually extended to Blake. Path: Gill Brook Trail.

routes.name: Seward Range herd path
routes.desc: Last peak along the Seward ridge; usually combined with Seward and Donaldson. Path: Blueberry Trail and Seward Range herd path. Starts at Corey's Road parking area.

routes.name: Phelps Trail from the Garden
routes.desc: Steep rock slab and an exposed summit make this one of the harder marked High Peaks; the Loj approach via Marcy Dam is longer. Path: Phelps Trail from The Garden. Starts at The Garden, Keene Valley.

routes.name: Van Hoevenberg Trail
routes.desc: The most popular route, marked all the way; the upper cone is bare rock and is followed by cairns and paint blazes. Path: Van Hoevenberg Trail. Starts at Adirondak Loj / High Peaks Information Center.

routes.name: Herbert Brook herd path
routes.desc: Marked trail to Flowed Lands, then a cairned herd path up Herbert Brook with many stream crossings. Path: Flowed Lands and Herbert Brook herd path. Starts at Upper Works, Newcomb.

routes.name: Uphill Brook herd path
routes.desc: Marked trail to the Uphill lean-to area, then a cairned herd path; the approach from the Loj crosses slides and is not the usual way. Path: Calamity Brook Trail to unmarked herd path. Starts at Upper Works, Newcomb.

routes.name: Via Mount Marcy
routes.desc: Usually climbed with Marcy and Gray; the alternative approach from Upper Works is longer. Path: Van Hoevenberg Trail over Marcy to Lake Tear of the Clouds. Starts at Adirondak Loj / High Peaks Information Center.

routes.name: Lake Arnold Trail
routes.desc: About 6.3 miles one way with roughly 2,500 ft of gain via Lake Arnold. The Avalanche Pass loop has been affected by slide damage, making the out-and-back the usual choice.

routes.name: Elk Pass Trail
routes.desc: Steep, sustained loop over Dial on the way down; reserve parking reservation needed in season. Path: Elk Pass trail from Lake Road, down the Leach Trail. Starts at St. Huberts parking (Adirondack Mountain Reserve).

routes.name: Via Indian Pass Brook
routes.desc: A short herd path from the same junction as Street Mountain, usually climbed with it. Path: Nye ski trail and herd path via Indian Pass Brook. Starts at Adirondak Loj / High Peaks Information Center.

routes.name: Panther Brook herd path
routes.desc: Unmarked path leaves the Bradley Pond trail about 4.3 miles in; often combined with Santanoni. Path: Bradley Pond Trail and Panther Brook herd path. Starts at Upper Works, Newcomb.

routes.name: Phelps Trail
routes.desc: Heavily used marked trail leaving the Marcy route past Marcy Dam; a good first High Peak. Path: Van Hoevenberg Trail and Phelps Trail. Starts at Adirondak Loj / High Peaks Information Center.

routes.name: Cascade Mountain Trail to Porter spur
routes.desc: Follow the Cascade trail about 2 miles to a junction, then turn right for roughly 0.7-0.8 miles to the summit. About 5 miles round trip.

routes.name: Via Giant Mountain
routes.desc: Most climbers go over Giant and along the ridge; a longer direct route starts at the East Trail on Route 9. Path: Roaring Brook Trail over Giant, then the ridge trail.

routes.name: Ore Bed Trail
routes.desc: Steps and ladders on the Ore Bed Trail; the garden lot is small and fills early on weekends. Path: Johns Brook Valley and Ore Bed Trail. Starts at The Garden, Keene Valley.

routes.name: Santanoni Express
routes.desc: Steep eroded herd path after the marked trail to Bradley Pond; Santanoni Brook can be hard to cross when wet. Path: Bradley Pond Trail and Santanoni Express herd path. Starts at Upper Works, Newcomb.

routes.name: Weld Trail
routes.desc: Out-and-back on a marked trail with a steep rock slab; the reserve needs a parking reservation in season. Path: Weld Trail. Starts at St. Huberts parking (Adirondack Mountain Reserve).

routes.name: Seward herd path
routes.desc: Marked trail for about 5 miles, then an unmarked eroded path; the road can be closed in winter. Path: Blueberry Trail to Seward herd path. Starts at Corey's Road parking area.

routes.name: Ward Brook herd path
routes.desc: Cairned herd path leaves the truck trail just past the Ward Brook lean-to; steep and slippery on top. Path: Blueberry Trail, Ward Brook Truck Trail and Seymour herd path. Starts at Corey's Road parking area.

routes.name: Dix Range herd path
routes.desc: Unmarked herd path with a steep dip and bare-rock climb; also called Carson Peak. Path: Dix Range crest herd path from Elk Lake. Starts at Elk Lake trailhead.

routes.name: Via Indian Pass Brook
routes.desc: Unmarked and brushy; the unbridged brook crossing can be dangerous at high water. Done with Nye in one trip. Path: Nye ski trail and herd path via Indian Pass Brook. Starts at Adirondak Loj / High Peaks Information Center.

routes.name: Herd path from the Van Hoevenberg Trail
routes.desc: Unmarked herd path leaving the main trail past Marcy Dam; frequently paired with Phelps. Path: Herd path off the Van Hoevenberg Trail. Starts at Adirondak Loj / High Peaks Information Center.

routes.name: Wedge Brook Trail
routes.desc: Steep and often icy on the upper part; a longer alternative starts at The Garden via Johns Brook. Path: West River Trail, Wedge Brook Trail and State Range Trail cutoff. Starts at St. Huberts parking (Adirondack Mountain Reserve).

routes.name: Wilmington Trail
routes.desc: About 5.2 miles one way with roughly 3,600-3,700 ft of gain, passing ski trails and lifts. A short unmarked side path branches off toward Esther Mountain.

routes.name: Wright Peak Spur Trail from Algonquin Trail
routes.desc: Take the Marcy Dam and Algonquin trails to the spur junction about 3.1 miles in, then climb a steep rock slab for 0.4 miles to the summit. About 7 miles round trip with roughly 2,600 ft of gain.

routes.name: Wy'East
routes.descent: Descend by the standard South Side route back to Timberline Lodge.

routes.name: South Side (Hogsback)
routes.descent: Descend the way you came, most parties reversing the Old Chute facing into the slope, then down the Hogsback and around Crater Rock to the ski area and back to the lodge. In poor visibility, a compass bearing that does not account for the fall line will pull descending parties off to the southwest onto the Zigzag Glacier and toward Mississippi Head, or southeast toward White River Canyon; carry a

routes.name: Cooper Spur
routes.descent: Avoid downclimbing the spur, which is the most dangerous part of the mountain to reverse. Most parties descend the standard south side to Timberline and arrange a car shuttle.

routes.name: Eliot Glacier Headwall
routes.descent: Descend the Sunshine route or a south side route.

routes.name: North Face Left Gully
routes.descent: The descent depends on where the car is. To return to Tilly Jane, descend Cooper Spur or the Sunshine Route, both on steep snow; the Sunshine Route has bergschrunds. To return to Timberline, take the South Side route.

routes.name: North Face Right Gully
routes.descent: Descend Cooper Spur or the Sunshine route back to the start, or go down the south side and arrange a car shuttle.

routes.name: Icefall Chute (Boy Scouts Chute)
routes.descent: Descend by whichever is safest, typically Old Chute or the Pearly Gates.

routes.name: Men of Steel
routes.descent: The top joins the Wy'East route and its variations, which lead to the summit. Alternatively, descend to the Devil's Kitchen by a variation such as the Flying Buttress or East Crater Wall.

routes.name: Steel Cliff South Face
routes.descent: Follow the standard Wy'East route down.

routes.name: Reid Glacier Headwall
routes.descent: Descend by the Old Chute, an easy ramp from the knife-edge rim into the crater.

routes.name: Sandy Glacier Headwall
routes.descent: Descend the South Side route.

routes.name: Yocum Ridge
routes.descent: Descend Leuthold Couloir, or go over the summit and down a standard South Side route.

routes.name: Full Richardson
routes.descent: From the summit, rappel to the west-northwest, then downclimb the northwest ridge to a north-facing slope and traverse east back to the gear left at the foot of the couloir. Parties who want to skip the summit pitches can also traverse right and descend earlier.

routes.name: Nine O'clock Gully
routes.descent: From the top of the gully there are two ways down: downclimb the gully itself, or hike across the crater rim and downclimb the neighbouring Eleven O'clock Gully, whichever looks easier on the day. Either gully needs solid snow cover to be in condition, and a cornice may cap the top of this one, so look it over from below before committing. Those continuing to the summit can cross the west face and

routes.name: Northwest Ridge
routes.descent: fastest and safest way down for every route on the mountain; the only route with no glacier travel

routes.name: Southeast Ridge
routes.descent: Do not try to drop the 8,000-8,200 ft cliff band on the northeast side when returning to Camp Lake; go back down the snow and scree you came up.

routes.name: West Rib
routes.descent: Reverse the ridge, or traverse north around the pinnacle to its east side and downclimb loose fourth-class rock from there. Rockfall is common.

routes.name: Southwest Ridge
routes.descent: Return to the Red Saddle, then plunge down the scree face between the southwest and south ridges and traverse back onto the southwest ridge around 8,000 ft. The pinnacle can be rappelled; the alternative is downclimbing loose fourth class.

routes.name: Whitewater Glacier
routes.descent: Reverse the route: downclimb or rappel the pinnacle, cross back over the Red Saddle traverse, then descend the scree and the glacier. Rockfall above the traverse increases once the afternoon sun warms the face.

routes.name: East Face aka "Brainless Child" (Tyler Adams Memorial Route)
Northeast Buttress (McLaughlin Memorial Route)
routes.descent: Finish by scrambling the summit block by its regular south line, then descend the West Ridge. Getting back depends on whether a car or bikes were left at the Mt. Thielsen trailhead or the party walked in from Diamond Lake.

routes.name: North Ridge
routes.descent: Downclimb easy rock or rappel from a slung boulder; two ropes reach the notch

routes.name: West Ridge
routes.descent: Come down the North Ridge: three rappels, and with a 50 m rope one short fourth-class downclimb remains after the second; avoid kicking scree onto parties below (July-August).

routes.name: East Buttress
routes.descent: Descend by the South Ridge route, the Southwest Ridge, or the early-morning couloir.

routes.name: Thayer Glacier Headwall
routes.descent: Retrace your route down, or go down the standard route.

routes.name: Southeast Ridge
routes.descent: Reverse the climb: downclimb or rappel the Bowling Alley, where rappel slings are usually in place, pass the pinnacles on their south side, and descend the ridge. Scree continues down to about 7,000 ft.

routes.name: North Face Couloir
routes.descent: Descend the North Ridge back to your camp, or carry your gear over the summit and go down the South Side.

routes.name: North Face of the Northwest Ridge
routes.descent: Descend the North Ridge back to your camp, or continue over the summit and go down the South Side.

routes.name: Silver Couloir
routes.descent: Descend the North Ridge back to your camp, or carry your gear over the summit and go down the South Side.

routes.name: South Side Route
routes.descent: Descend the way you came, down the South Sister Climbers Trail to the Devils Lake trailhead. The upper trail is loose volcanic scree and cinder that slides underfoot, and with snow cover an ice axe and crampons may be needed. Parties who loop through Moraine Lake instead face a steep, slippery trail into the canyon, with a rugged first stretch that needs hands.

routes.name: South Ridge Route
routes.descent: reverse the route

routes.name: Stolen Chimney
routes.descent: three rappels, crossing back over the narrow crest to the three-bolt belay

routes.name: Black Sun
routes.descent: descend the northern side with either two 200 ft doubled-rope raps or four 100 ft raps, or four doubled-rope raps down the standard line

routes.name: Burning Inside
routes.descent: descend the northern side with either two 200 ft doubled-rope raps or four 100 ft raps

routes.name: Kor-Ingalls Route
routes.descent: rap the route in four pitches, or better, descend the northern side with either two 200 ft doubled-rope raps or four 100 ft raps

routes.name: The Bjornstad Traverse ( The Girdle of Castleton Tower)
West Face
routes.descent: single rappel using two ropes off summit anchors

routes.name: Vision Quest
routes.descent: three double-rope rappels of about 150 ft down the east face

routes.name: North Ridge
routes.descent: four or five double-rope rappels down the route

routes.name: Pale Fire
routes.descent: four rappels with doubled ropes down the line, or five down a south-face line

routes.name: Where have the Wild Things Gone
South Face
routes.descent: two rappels

routes.name: Crack Wars
routes.descent: two long double-rope rappels down the route, or rap one of the neighbouring lines

routes.name: Empirical Route
routes.descent: two double-rope rappels from the chained anchors

routes.name: Fine Jade
routes.descent: three rappels down the route

routes.name: Finger of Fatwa
routes.descent: From the top, join the Middle Finger Buttress-Left descent line: traverse east to the col southwest of the North Ridge and downclimb the 3rd-class north-slope gully back to the approach trail.

routes.name: Middle Finger Buttress - Left Side
routes.descent: From the top of the buttress, walk east along the ridge crest to the small col located southwest of the North Ridge, then downclimb the 3rd-class gully on the north slope back toward the approach trail.

routes.name: Middle Finger Buttress - Right Side
routes.descent: From the top, traverse east along the ridge crest to the col southwest of the North Ridge and downclimb the 3rd-class north-slope gully back toward the approach trail.

routes.name: North Ridge
routes.descent: From the summit plateau, either reverse toward Cathedral Pass and drop southwest around the mountain to Upper Cathedral Lake, or head to a small col just southwest of the North Ridge and downclimb a 3rd-class gully on the north slope back toward the approach.

routes.name: Pilgrimage to Mecca
routes.descent: From the top of the route, hike east to gain the saddle area of Amphitheater Mountain, then follow the descent trail/slopes south back down to Upper Cathedral Lake to rejoin the approach.

routes.name: West Route
routes.descent: From the summit plateau, descend the same scree/grass slopes back into the west basin, then follow the boot path down to the trail and back to Upper Cathedral Lake. Parties combining with Cathedral Peak often traverse between the two via a connecting gully rather than returning all the way to the lake between summits.

routes.name: Southeast Ridge
routes.descent: From the true summit, scramble back east along the summit ridge to the top of the South Gully. Its one technical step is a short, blocky rock cleft capped by a chockstone, with a fixed sling above it: rappel it or downclimb it on belay. Below that, descend the long gully and the brushy, forested slope beneath it toward Ingalls Creek, return to camp, and reverse the approach over Fourth Creek Pass

routes.name: Northeast Couloir
routes.descent: Retrace your steps from the summit to the upper rock band, then make one rappel onto the ledge on the southeast face; you may need to rig a natural anchor, and one party used a slung tree there. Then head over to the top of the Northeast Couloir and find the gully just east of it: two or three single-rope rappels down that gully reach the snow slopes below. Anchors are natural and not reliably in

routes.name: Northwest Arete
routes.descent: Do not expect to simply reverse the arete pitch-for-pitch — the standard descent traverses off to the east side of the mountain and down to the Argonaut-Colchuck col, and it typically takes about 4 rappels: from near the top of the route, a rappel (a single 60 m rope reaches) down the upper northeast-face snowfield; a short scramble to a tree anchor for the next rappel down more broken, more reaso

routes.name: South Face
routes.descent: Descend by reversing the ascent gully. The single technical obstacle is the 50-foot chockstone gully near the top: rappel it rather than downclimbing (a webbing/sling anchor is typically found immediately above the chockstone — inspect and consider backing it up with fresh webbing, as reports note it sees heavy wear). A 40 m rope is ideal for this rappel and a 30 m rope will also reach; be careful

routes.name: Austera Peak
routes.descent: Reverse the route: climb back up the ~75 ft rappel pitch (well-protected 5.5), navigate the moat, retrace the north ridge/McAllister Glacier traverse back through Klawatti Col, and cross the Inspiration Glacier back to camp.

routes.name: Southwest Ridge / McAllister Glacier
routes.descent: Descent reverses the same glacier traverse and is not a simple walk-off — expect real rappelling on the technical sections. From the summit, the standard line down is the same chimney/chockstone gully used on the ascent (rated roughly 5.2, about 60 ft): parties commonly rappel this in two rappels using anchors already in place at the top of the chockstone gully (slung horns/chockstones — treat as

routes.name: South Ridge / Southwest Gully
routes.descent: Descend by reversing the ascent line: down the summit gully to the 7,400-ft shoulder, back across the ducked/cairned rib-and-gully traverse to Azurite Pass, and down the Mill Creek/Azurite Pass climbers' trail to Horse Heaven Camp and the PCT/West Fork Methow Trail back to the trailhead. This is a walk-off/downclimb for the majority of parties in normal summer, dry-rock conditions — no fixed rappe

routes.name: Standard Scramble
routes.descent: This is a walk-off/downclimb descent with no rappelling — retrace the southeast ridge/rib line used on ascent. Favor climber's right on the upper scree and rock band, where footing is comparatively firmer and there's less rockfall exposure onto anyone below; the loose 'garbage' talus here is the descent's main hazard, particularly when dry and off-trail. Several trip reports specifically note that

routes.name: Beckey-Tate
routes.descent: Do not plan to rappel the Beckey-Tate line itself — while it's technically possible with two ropes (roughly five or six rappels off slings and trees), the route wanders and holds a lot of large loose rock, making rope-stuck and rockfall risk high; most parties explicitly avoid it. Instead, from the top of the route scramble about 20 ft up and left to reach the notch that separates the south face f

routes.name: Going Down Under
routes.descent: From the top of the route, join the standard descent: scramble to the notch just north of the true summit, then follow the loose scree-and-snow gully back down toward the Hairpin pullout, roughly two hours from the top.

routes.name: Kearney-Thomas
routes.descent: As with the neighboring Beckey-Tate line, descend by scrambling to the notch just north of the true summit and following the loose scree-and-snow gully back down toward the Hairpin pullout, roughly two hours from the top.

routes.name: Skinny Start
routes.descent: The standard descent is the Beckey-Tate walk-down (scramble to the notch, then the loose gully back to the Hairpin pullout). Rappelling the Beckey-Tate line itself is the other option, but at least one party was unable to find a rappel anchor along the top of that line and instead had to change into rock shoes and make a high traverse to a saddle before descending — budget extra time and be prepar

routes.name: Walkabout
routes.descent: The first-ascent team bivied on the summit after topping out at 2 a.m. and descended the following morning via the Beckey-Tate line — scrambling to the notch just north of the summit, then following the loose scree-and-snow gully back toward the Hairpin pullout (roughly two hours from the summit).

routes.name: West Face / West Route
routes.descent: The route's final move is the crux of the whole outing: an exposed, essentially unprotected 5.6 slab move past a single old, rusty 1/4-inch bolt to the tiny summit. This is downclimbed or top-roped back to the belay stance rather than rappelled — there's no real anchor up top to rap from, and space on the summit is too small for a stance. From that belay/notch, two slung-block (tat) anchors serve

routes.name: West Ridge (Standard Route)
routes.descent: From the summit, downclimb about 10 ft to a rappel anchor and rappel the short friction slab, then downclimb/scramble back to the top of the lower chimney and rappel (existing webbing/anchors reported) to the ridge below. From there, descend the class 2 west ridge back to the upper basin, retrace the scree/snow traverse, and descend the Willow Creek drainage (loose, brushy) back to the SR-20 pullo

routes.name: Northeast Ridge
routes.descent: From the summit, work down and south toward the South Ridge route, using one rappel or a down-climb to get below the initial band of rock, then continuing south to the south col. From there the descent follows the South Ridge's loose, cairned gully (described by multiple parties as tedious and 'choss'-prone) back down to snow slopes and Wing Lake. Some parties glissade the snow lower down early in

routes.name: South Ridge
routes.descent: This is the standard descent line for the peak — no separate down-route to learn. The ascent from the south col follows the cairned ridge (some class 3 moves) and a loose gully just west of the crest to the summit pyramid; the final section is a cairned class 2 ledge system traversing below the summit block that is exposed near its end, followed by a short (~15 ft) class 4 step to the true summit.

routes.name: Standard Scramble
routes.descent: This is a scramble with no rappelling — descend by reversing the ascent line. From the black-hornfels summit, downclimb the northeast ridge (Class 2-3, loose in spots) back down to the east-face scree/talus, which is noticeably looser and more hazardous descending than ascending — plan on a slow, controlled downclimb with attention to kicking rock onto anyone below. Continue down the scree/talus t

routes.name: Cascadian Route
routes.descent: From the Southwest Summit, downclimb/traverse to the Isella Glacier and descend along an undulating line of steep rock and moraine at about two-thirds of the glacier's height, then cross through a notch in the south ridge to regain the North Star-Bonanza col camp.

routes.name: Mary Green Glacier (Standard Route)
routes.descent: Reverse the route: down-climb the summit ridge and rocky rib back toward the glacier, staying climber's left of the standard line to dodge rockfall funneling down the gullies. The established descent uses 6–7 fixed rappel stations (horns, flakes, and slung boulders left by prior parties) along the class 3–4 rock band, typically consolidated into about four rappels using a 60m x 8mm rope — a common

routes.name: Northeast Buttress
routes.descent: The straightforward descent reverses down to the Mary Green Glacier and follows the standard route's descent: down-climb the summit ridge/rock rib, use the fixed rappel stations through the class 3–4 band (about four rappels with a 60m rope, 8mm lines are common), cross the moat, and descend the glacier to Holden Pass camp — see the Mary Green Glacier route's descent notes for full detail on that

routes.name: Oregonian Route
routes.descent: The route ends on the southwest summit (about 9,320 ft) after merging with the upper Soviet Route, and the way down is the same as for that route. Follow the crest northeast to the West Peak, which takes close to two hours because the gendarmes are mostly bypassed on third and fourth class ledges with one short rappel. From the West Peak, downclimb talus on the northwest side to a band of steep sl

routes.name: Northwest Ridge (from Needle Peak)
routes.descent: This is a long ridge traverse that links Needle Peak, Dark Peak and the crest to Bonanza, so there is no easy retreat once committed; the way down is from the Bonanza summit ridge by the Mary Green Glacier route. routes.name: Soviet Route
routes.descent: From the Southwest Peak (route's high point), traverse the Northeast Ridge to the West Peak — about 2 hours, negotiating a series of gendarmes mostly on 3rd/4th-class ledges, with one short rappel along the way. From the West Peak, descend the northwest side: downclimb talus, then make two rappels of roughly 200 feet each down steep slabs back into the approach basin. Anchors on this descent have

routes.name: Southeast Face
routes.descent: Descend by reversing the approach to the summit ridge, then rappel rather than downclimb the loose upper face: from the summit, walk a few feet toward Sahale to the first rappel sling/station. Three rappels down the southeast/east face bring you back to the snow at the head of the Boston Glacier, near the base of the Sahale–Boston col. Multiple independent trip-report accounts describe the anchors

routes.name: Northwest Ridge
routes.descent: No descent-only beta exists for this ridge — the first-ascent party continued their traverse onward (over to Sahale Peak and down Sahale Arm) rather than retreating back down it, so going down this way is undescribed. A party that climbed the ridge and topped out on Boston's summit would most sensibly descend via the Southeast Face route's established rappel line (3 rappels down the southeast/east

routes.name: South Ridge
routes.descent: This is a walk-off/downclimb - no rappelling is involved on the standard South Ridge route. Reverse the ascent line: downclimb the Class 2-3 (locally 3-4 near the summit horn) loose, rubbly schist back down the ridge crest to the low-angle snowfield/basin around 7,400 ft, then descend the pumice and talus slopes back to the Louis Creek Basin camp (~6,700 ft). From there, traverse back east below L

routes.name: North Face
routes.descent: The standard descent does not reverse the North Face — parties continue over the summit and go down Buckner's southwest slopes. From the top, descend gullies, scree, and snow on the fall line to about 7,200 ft, then traverse down and right across Horseshoe Basin on a broad ledge system at 6,200-6,400 ft (passing near the old Davenport Mine) to a snow finger; ascend the snow finger about 100 ft to

routes.name: Southwest Face / Southwest Slopes
routes.descent: Descend the same southwest-slopes line used on ascent — this is a walk-off/downclimb route with no rappelling required (rappels: 0). From the summit, downclimb the scree/rubble and re-descend the cowskull snowfield and chute on the fall line to about 7,200 ft; steep snow here is typically managed by facing in and plunge-stepping or downclimbing with an ice-axe self-belay, and less experienced part

routes.name: Northeast Ridge
routes.descent: From the summit, head to Prusik Pass and follow the standard route's trail through the Upper Enchantment Basin, down Aasgard Pass, and down the Mountaineer Creek/Colchuck Lake Trail back to the Stuart Lake Trailhead. This is a demanding ~15-mile loop with sustained class 3 scrambling and bushwhacking on the ascent, requiring at least 12 hours car-to-car and an early start.

routes.name: Northwest Ridge
routes.descent: Most parties retrace the route; a longer alternative heads east across the Druid Plateau, over Prusik Pass, through the Enchantments and down Aasgard Pass.

routes.name: South Slopes
routes.descent: Descend by reversing the ascent line: downclimb the exposed friction-slab ramp off the summit block (often the psychological crux of the day, since downclimbing low-angle slab is harder to read than ascending it), cross back over the Druid Plateau, and pick your way back down the talus/scree slopes to the rib at ~7,900-8,000 ft. From there reverse the contouring traverse at 7,300-7,400 ft past the

routes.name: Northwest Couloir–North Ridge
routes.descent: Reverse the ridge/couloir, or descend the east/southeast slopes if that side was used to finish the climb.

routes.name: Southeast Slopes
routes.descent: This is a walk-down/downclimb — no rope work or anchors are needed on the Southeast Slopes line. Reverse the ascent: downclimb the loose scree gully from the notch back into the upper basin, then pick your way back down through talus and sparse forest to rejoin the North Fork Entiat Trail near the Pyramid Mountain Trail junction (~6,600 ft). From there it's a straightforward trail descent down the

routes.name: SE Route
routes.descent: Reverse the ascent. Downclimb the SE gully, mostly class 2-3, staying in the main gully rather than drifting left onto harder ground, which is easy to do in fog. At the foot of the gullies a snowfield leads down; early in the season it is firm in the morning and may call for crampons, and by afternoon it softens enough to boot-ski or plunge-step. routes.name: West Ridge
routes.descent: Descend by reversing the West Ridge exactly as ascended: downclimb the northwest-facing summit gully back to the ~8,200 ft contour, follow the ridge back down through the same notches/gendarmes to the 8,000 ft west col, then drop SSW back to the ~7,100 ft camp/cross-country section and rejoin the Trail #1554/Windy Pass trail. From there retrace the Eightmile–Trout Creek Trail past Lake Caroline an

routes.name: Standard Scramble
routes.descent: There is no rappelling on this route — it is a walk-off/downclimb descent that simply reverses the ascent line. From the summit, downclimb the class 2-3 ground back to the notch on the southwest ridge at ~7,600 ft, then descend the same steep heather/talus/scree slope back into the Freezeout Creek drainage. This is the point where parties get into trouble: the upper basin has several gullies and c

routes.name: South Route
routes.descent: Reverse the ascent line back through the notch, northeast gully and south gully to Castle Creek Basin camp.

routes.name: The Drawbridge
routes.descent: Descend the south side of the peak and the East Ridge back toward camp; the first-ascent party described this walk-off as straightforward ('breezy'), regaining camp near twilight.

routes.name: Fight or Flight
routes.descent: From the top of the route, descend via Castle Peak's east ridge to an obvious col, then down a snow finger back toward the approach glacier/basin, rather than reversing the climbing line.

routes.name: Last Rites
routes.descent: From the summit, reverse the Southwest Route. The immediate obstacle is the long chasm that cleaves the summit rocks into north and south sections: you must cross back over it at the 'step-across', stepping onto a chockstone wedged in the slot and mantling a bulge. It is objectively an easy move with enormous exposure, and most parties belay or rig a handline with prusiks for it, especially with a

routes.name: Southeast Buttress
routes.descent: This is a walk-off — there is no established rappel line down the buttress, and multiple independent trip reports (2016, 2018, 2024) confirm parties descend unroped. From the summit, downclimb/scramble west and then southwest along third-class ledges on the peak's west side, aiming to regain the notch/gap system below the true summit block often called the 'summit chasm.' This gap must be crossed

routes.name: Southwest Route
routes.descent: Reverse the route. The step-across is the crux in both directions and is arguably harder going down, since you are stepping onto the chockstone with the exposure in front of you rather than behind; a handline with prusiks is the standard solution and belaying it is entirely reasonable. Lower down, a cannonhole gives an easier alternative to one vertical step you may have climbed on the way up. Bel

routes.name: NE Ridge
routes.descent: From the summit, downclimb/walk off to the west along the regular walk-up (SW slope) descent route used by all Cathedral Peak climbs; a short rappel may help getting off the summit ridge itself.

routes.name: South Face
routes.descent: Descend west off the summit via the regular class-3 walk-up route, the same descent used by the NE Ridge route; involves loose talus and some downclimbing back toward camp.

routes.name: Little Giant Pass – Luahna Col Route
routes.descent: Downclimb the loose summit scramble to the ridge/gully, traverse back below the north ridge past the Pilz Glacier's margin, drop into and cross the Napeequa Valley, then regain Little Giant Pass (6,409 ft) and descend the trail to the Chiwawa River ford and trailhead.

routes.name: Southwest Face
routes.descent: Downclimb the south slope/southwest face (same snow/scramble terrain, including the loose cliff band around 5,500-6,500 ft) back into Chalangin Basin, then retrace the Thunder Creek bushwhack and White River Trail to the trailhead; some parties vary the exit via Lower Thunder Meadows.

routes.name: Southwest Route / Standard
routes.descent: Descend by reversing the ascent line: down the southwest scree/gully slopes to the 6,300 ft bench, staying off the looser climber's-left skyline gully in favor of the main descent gullies/vegetated slopes used on the way up.
