routes.name: Walrus Glacier
routes.descent: Reverse the ascent line back to Boulder Creek Basin camp, then out via Boulder Creek Trail #1562 and White River Trail #1507 to the trailhead. If you climbed via the Walrus Glacier, descend the same glacier line back down to the 6,700 ft bench and over Boulder Pass, staying roped through the crevassed sections and unroping once back on stable moraine/talus below the ice. If you climbed/are descend

routes.name: Colchuck Glacier
routes.descent: This is a walk-off — no rappels. Reverse the ascent line: descend the glacier (staying climber's left, away from the thin crevasse zone that has opened as the glacier has retreated) and back down the lateral moraine to Colchuck Lake, then follow the Colchuck Lake Trail and Stuart Lake Trail back to the trailhead. In early season with good snow cover, much of the glacier and the upper trail basin c

routes.name: Holsten-Hilden
routes.descent: From the top of the route, join the standard East Route line and descend the Colchuck Glacier back toward Colchuck Col and Colchuck Lake, then follow the approach trail out.

routes.name: North Buttress Couloir
routes.descent: Descend the backside of the mountain onto the Colchuck Glacier and follow its standard route and the moraine back to Colchuck Lake; in soft, late-day snow this descent has been reported as slow and exhausting.

routes.name: Northeast Couloir
routes.descent: Standard descent is the walk-off: from the summit, traverse/downclimb to the Colchuck–Dragontail col (Colchuck Col, also called Banshee Pass) and descend the Colchuck Glacier's east/true-right lobe back to the basin above Colchuck Lake, then reverse the approach trail — the same line used to descend the Colchuck Glacier route. This is the recommended way down; reversing through the Northeast Coulo

routes.name: Northeast Buttress
routes.descent: This is a walk-off, not a rappel descent: from the summit plateau, downclimb/traverse to Colchuck–Dragontail Col (Colchuck Col/Banshee Pass) and descend the Colchuck Glacier's east/true-right lobe — the same standard line used to descend the Colchuck Glacier route — back into the basin above Colchuck Lake, then follow the boot path and trail out. Staying on the glacier's margin (rather than its ce

routes.name: Cosley-Houston Couloir
routes.descent: Cosley-Houston is a walk-off, not a rappel descent. From the summit area, follow the boot track (or break a new one) toward Colfax's secondary/eastern summit, then contour around its south side just below the top — no technical downclimbing is required on a normal-conditions descent. This drops you to the Colfax-Baker col (the Baker-Colfax saddle). From the saddle, pick up the standard Coleman-Dem

routes.name: Ford's Theatre
routes.descent: Walk-off via the Coleman-Deming route (as for the Cosley-Houston, which this route joins near the top), no rappels.

routes.name: Kimchi Suicide Volcano
routes.descent: The route finishes on easy snow and ice slopes to the summit of Colfax Peak, and the way down is a walk-off with no rappels. Cross the Colfax-Baker col behind the summit and pick up the standard Coleman-Deming route down the Coleman Glacier, as for the neighboring routes on this face. Stay roped for the glacier and expect the same crevasses you passed on the way in. Follow the lateral moraine to t

routes.name: Polish Route
routes.descent:
The way down is on foot, not by rappel: from the top, continue to the Colfax-Baker saddle and descend the Coleman Glacier, the same walk-off used from the neighbouring lines on this face.

routes.name: South Route
routes.descent: Nearly all parties reverse the ascent line (Southeast Glacier / upper Northeast Ridge route) rather than finding a separate walk-off: downclimb the Class 3 ridge (one short, more exposed Class 3+/4 move is commonly reported near the summit ridge, and some parties carry a short hand line for one airy notch — this is a fixed handline, not a rappel) back to the north-side notch, downclimb (or belay,

routes.name: Standard Scramble
routes.descent: This is a scramble, not a technical rock route, and no rappels are used — descend by reversing the ascent line. From the summit, downclimb the class 2-4 upper section back to the saddle (accounts vary on the exact character here: some parties describe a short, fun class 2-3 scramble from a notch just below the true summit; others describe roughly 250 vertical feet of class 3-4 terrain near the top

routes.name: Standard Scramble
routes.descent: Descend by reversing the ascent line exactly: downclimb the class 2+ boulder field below the summit back onto the boot path, then follow the use trail down the southeast ridge to Fish Creek Pass. From the pass, rejoin the West Fork Buttermilk Trail #411 for the full hike back down to the trailhead. This is a walk-off/downclimb the entire way — there is no rappelling on the standard route, and most

routes.name: Southeast Ridge
routes.descent: Descend the same way you came up: reverse the west-ridge/west-flank ledge system back down to the 7,500 ft col, then drop into the Bird Lakes basin and follow Bird Creek back down through the 5,400 ft high camp to Bird Creek Camp and the maintained Devore Creek Trail to Weaver Point. This is fundamentally a downclimb, not a rappel-dependent descent — most of the Class 3-4 terrain is downclimbed in

routes.name: Dome Glacier
routes.descent: Descend by reversing the ascent line: down the rock arête (~500 ft) back to the notch at 8,560 ft, then down the snow slope (~300 ft) onto the Dome Glacier, and back down-glacier along the ascent track to the base of the climb, retracing the cross-country traverse back to high camp. The rock arête itself is narrow, exposed, and largely featureless — many parties belay or fix a handline/rappel for

routes.name: Indian Summer
routes.descent: The technical climbing ends just below the top, and a short scramble reaches the summit. From there the way down is brief: a few minutes of walking and easy downclimbing returns to the saddle between Dome and Chickamin Peaks, where parties camp on snow beside the Dome Glacier. routes.name: Direct Southwest Buttress
routes.descent: The Direct start rejoins the standard Southwest Buttress after its first two pitches, so the descent is the same as the standard route's: from the top, return to the head of the approach gully and make a single-rope rappel (climbers may need to downclimb or work around an open moat at the bottom). Alternatively, from a large rock on the ridge about 10 meters north of the true summit, a fixed rappe

routes.name: East Ridge / Inspiration Glacier
routes.descent: From the summit, avoid old/misleading rappel tat and head toward the Northwest Ridge. Locate a wrapped-block rappel anchor a short distance above a stance; rappel roughly 30m (100 ft) to another stance, then scramble easy ledges to a further, uncomplicated rappel that lands in a moatless notch. From there, navigate steep crevasses on climber's right to regain the McAllister-Inspiration col and the

routes.name: Northwest Ridge
routes.descent: Descend by downclimbing or rappelling the same Northwest Ridge line used on ascent. A single rappel down the final snow/rock step back to the glacier is typical, though parties sometimes downclimb this section instead if conditions allow; a 30m rope suffices for the short rock pitches, but bring a 60m single if you intend to rappel the snow pitch in one go rather than making two shorter raps. routes.name: Southwest Buttress
routes.descent: From the summit, downclimb/scramble a short distance to a large rock/boulder on the ridge about 10 meters north of the true summit, where a fixed rappel ring and sling (recently reported as reinforced with an additional sling) anchors the route's single rappel: a double-rope rappel (both strands, ~60m rope) that lowers you to a steep snow slope which, in normal-season conditions, keeps a solid con

routes.name: Der Dihedral
routes.descent: There is almost no descent-specific beta for Der Dihedral beyond the fact that it joins the 1972 NE Arete to finish. Since the route tops out on the same upper mountain terrain as Backbone Ridge, the standard descent is the same walk-off used for that route and for the summit generally: scramble/snow traverse southeast to a saddle, then east across the long snow slope to Aasgard Pass, and down the

routes.name: Backbone Ridge
routes.descent: Most parties descend the east ledges and sandy summit gully toward Aasgard Pass and down to Colchuck Lake. When the upper descent gully is icy (common late season), rappel instead — two rappels on a 70m rope (60m works) using rock anchors to avoid the ice slope, with a documented rappel station near 47.479°N, 120.832°W. Watch for loose rock and verify anchor integrity on any rappel here — parties

routes.name: East Ridge via Aasgard Pass Route
routes.descent: It is a common and dangerous mistake for fatigued parties to veer too far climber's-right on the Aasgard Pass descent into steep, cliffed-out terrain — stay on the cairned line trending climber's-left. A slide on the steep upper pass could carry a climber into boulders below; icy conditions here have contributed to serious falls and fatalities.

routes.name: Gerber-Sink
routes.descent: Parties who top out into the upper Triple Couloirs exit typically continue, unroped, down the standard boot-packed couloir/gully system used to descend Triple Couloirs, then continue to Aasgard Pass and descend its snow slope (glissading is common) back to Colchuck Lake - one documented winter ascent finished exactly this way, unroped after the couloir and glissading most of Aasgard Pass. This is

routes.name: Pandora's Box (W Couloir)
routes.descent: From the top of the couloir/Pandora's Box, descend left and traverse northeast to the true summit (some parties rope up for this exposed traverse), or alternatively exit about 30 ft below the notch, scramble Class 4 rock roughly 20 ft, and follow the ridge left to the top. From the summit, the standard descent is southeast to a saddle, then east across a long snow slope to Aasgard Pass, then down

routes.name: Triple Couloirs
routes.descent: From the top of the third couloir, a short snow scramble reaches the summit. Traverse to the true summit, then make a long descending traverse across the upper snowfields toward Asgard Pass, and descend the pass's gully back to the frozen/open lake and the approach trail. In late February the descent from the summit is a plunge-step down the backside in snow, reaching Colchuck Lake after dark if t

routes.name: Serpentine Arête
routes.descent: From the summit, most parties head down the loose sandy gully shared with the top of Backbone Ridge, boot-ski or downclimb the upper Snow Creek Glacier snowfield where present, then traverse to Aasgard Pass (7,841 ft) and descend its steep, loose talus/scree back to Colchuck Lake. Crampons and an ice axe are important for this descent whenever snow/ice remain on the upper mountain or in Aasgard Pa

routes.name: This, My Friend
routes.descent: From the top, traverse south and west across broken 3rd/4th class terrain, losing elevation gradually until reaching a clean gully roughly 500 ft below the final belay. Descend the gully to a large ledge, then scramble southwest to walkable ground where you intersect the standard summit descent trail down to Aasgard Pass; follow the cairned, braided climbers' trail down the pass's steep talus/snow

routes.name: West Route / Standard Scramble
routes.descent: Descent is a reversal of the ascent line, down the west ridge and the ledge/gully system back into the south-facing basin above Phelps Basin — there is no fixed rappel gear anywhere on the route and no rappelling is required in normal (mid-to-late-summer) conditions. From the summit, downclimb the Class 3 west ridge scrambling back to the ledges; parties note it's easy to end up above short cliff

routes.name: East Ridge (Inspiration Glacier)
routes.descent: Reverse the ascent line: downclimb the exposed, corniced knife-edge summit ridge (in certain conditions a very thin edge with steep — 40–45°+ — flanks; ice axe and crampons essentially mandatory, and rope/running-belay technique is common for less experienced members), continue down through the gap in the lower East Ridge, then rope up again to cross the Inspiration Glacier and descend the Eldorad

routes.name: Northwest Couloir / Eldorado Glacier
routes.descent: From the summit, do not reverse the couloir — descend via the standard East Ridge / Inspiration Glacier route: downclimb the knife-edge summit ridge, drop through the gap in the lower East Ridge, rope up and cross the Inspiration Glacier, then descend the Eldorado Glacier back toward Roush Basin and Eldorado Creek Basin, finishing on the timbered climbers' trail back to the Cascade River crossing

routes.name: North Ridge
routes.descent: Return down the same ridge system to the notch and back to camp on the Inspiration Glacier; parties who finish via the East Ridge instead descend that ridge's knife-edge back to camp.

routes.name: Northeast Face
routes.descent: Descend the standard East Ridge rather than the face. Downclimb the knife-edge summit ridge, which can be icy and firm late in the season, and drop through the gap in the lower ridge to the Inspiration Glacier. Rope up for the glacier, then follow the standard track down the Eldorado Glacier to Roush Basin, over the intervening ridge into Eldorado Creek Basin, and down the boulder field and timber

routes.name: West Arete
routes.descent: From the summit, descend the East Ridge — most parties find this significantly easier and more straightforward than downclimbing the loose West Arete — then return to camp via the Inspiration/Eldorado Glacier.

routes.name: Tepeh Towers
routes.descent: From the summit, downclimb or rappel from a fixed rappel station directly below the top, landing back on the glacier for the return traverse to camp.

routes.name: South Ridge
routes.descent: Descend via Eldorado's standard East Ridge route back toward the glacier camp.

routes.name: Southeast Ridge
routes.descent: Descend by reversing the southeast ridge/gully line used on ascent: downclimb class 2–3 terrain from the summit block back to the notch in the upper basin between Saska and Emerald, then follow the gully back down to the 6,900 ft basin and re-cross the shoulder to the camp flat near 7,000–7,100 ft. This is a walk-off/downclimb — no fixed anchors or rappel stations are reported on this route, and p

routes.name: West Route
routes.descent: Downclimb from the summit block back through the class 3 gully on the west side, taking care on the steep slab near the south summit and the East Face exposure; regain the basin and retrace either the North Fork Entiat or Emerald Park Trail approach.

routes.name: East Ridge (Prusik Pass)
routes.descent: Downclimb the short 3rd-class step off the summit block carefully, then walk the ridge's minor humps back east to Prusik Pass. From there, descend the same way you came in — either back over Aasgard Pass to Colchuck Lake, or out via the Snow Lakes trail if approached from that side.

routes.name: South Gully
routes.descent: Reverse the ascent line. This route tops out on the northeast summit, which a 2023 survey confirms is the true high point, and its descent is a walk-off: downclimb the short, loose 3rd-class gully off the summit plateau — the same step you came up — then reverse the cross-country traverse back through the Reginleif/Sigrun tarn basin to the top of Aasgard Pass. Downclimbing Aasgard Pass is the desc

routes.name: Southwest Slope (Standard Route)
routes.descent: Down-climb the southwest ridge/slope on the same loose talus and scree used for the ascent, back to the saddle south of Enigma Peak, then drop and re-cross upper Castle Creek before regaining the bushwhack corridor down to Bird Creek Camp. The loose, sometimes football-sized talus is reported as noticeably more tedious and unstable on descent than ascent — expect slower travel and watch for rock k

routes.name: East Ledges
routes.descent: The usual descent is the ascent line reversed. From a horn near the summit, make the first of five single-rope rappels (roughly 400 ft total) down the northeast side to a series of ledges, then follow the ledges east - mostly 3rd class with short 4th-class moves at rib crossings - across roughly five rock ribs before a short gully leads back up to the East Ridge crest near the solitary gendarme. T

routes.name: East Ridge Direct
routes.descent: The East Ridge is not reversed as a rappel line in its own right; two descents are used instead. The standard one is the East Ledges, dropping climber's-right/northeast directly off the summit: three rappels trend northeast from the summit area, then a short, exposed grassy traverse east to the next rock rib, followed by two more rappels onto the East Ledges proper, about 5 rappels in all. From th

routes.name: North Ridge
routes.descent: The North Ridge finishes on the summit, and the way off is the West Ridge. Downclimb and rappel the West Ridge to the notch (one rope is enough for the rappels, and several anchors exist, so the mix is a matter of choice), then downclimb or rappel the snow couloir below the notch into Boston Basin; the Cat Scratch Gully to the climber's left is a rappel alternative. Allow more time than expected,

routes.name: Northeast Face
routes.descent: Do not reverse the Northeast Face. Most parties descend by the West Ridge, as below; the East Ledges off the northeast side are the faster but looser, harder-to-follow alternative. From the true summit, downclimb back past the false summit to the crux tower, then work down the West Ridge crest with exposed 3rd/4th-class downclimbing and about 3 rappels off slung horns and blocks, back to the notch

routes.name: Northwest Face
routes.descent: Do not reverse the Northwest Face; descend by the standard West Ridge. From the true summit, downclimb back past the false summit to the crux tower, then work down the West Ridge crest with exposed 3rd/4th-class downclimbing and about 3 rappels off slung horns and blocks, back to the West Ridge notch. From the notch, downclimb a short section of 3rd-class rock to the first station of the Cat Scrat

routes.name: West Ridge
routes.descent: There is no walk-off. Descend the way you came up as far as the notch, then take the rock gullies beside the couloir. From the true summit, downclimb back past the false summit to the crux tower, then work down the ridge crest with exposed 3rd/4th-class downclimbing and about 3 rappels off slung horns and blocks, back to the West Ridge notch. From the notch, downclimb a short section of 3rd-class

routes.name: East Ridge
routes.descent: From the summit, follow the East Ridge crest back, down-climbing the chimney step partway along it, to the head of the loose gully, descending it carefully to the ~7,200 ft col. From the col, either continue on to Chiwawa Mountain (a common combined objective) or drop back to the ~6,300 ft bench and retrace the cross-country line down to the Chiwawa River Trail, then out via the Buck Creek Trail t

routes.name: Northeast Face
routes.descent: Follow the ridge crest down from the summit; locate the chimney carefully, as at least one party missed it near an 8,500' col where the direct line was too steep and crossed onto the east face instead. In winter/spring the ridge can be corniced in places and holds steep snow requiring careful downclimbing or a short rope.

routes.name: Southwest Face
routes.descent: From the summit, retrace the ascent line down the south ridge / upper southwest face. The direct gully is the loosest ground on the mountain; a 2015 party found and cairned an alternate class 3 line over more solid, blocky terrain to skier's right of the gully that later parties have followed. Continue down through scree and talus to the grassy benches above Pass No Pass, back over the pass, and d

routes.name: South Slopes
routes.descent: This is a non-technical alpine scramble — the standard West Ridge / Saddle Traverse descent involves no rappelling (0 rappels). From Gardner's summit the route continues west along the summit ridge over a false summit, then descends steeply through loose scree and (early-season) snow to a saddle below Point 8487. From that saddle, the crest up to Point 8487 has gendarmes and cliff bands that go at

routes.name: Disappointment Peak Cleaver (Gerdine Ridge / Cool Glacier)
routes.descent: No rappelling; reverse the ascent line on foot. From the summit, descend the ridge to the 9,600 ft col, then down the Cool Glacier to the 9,100 ft col. On the traverse back beneath Disappointment Peak, keep lower and farther from the face than on the way in to cut the time spent under its rockfall. Crevasses on the Cool Glacier open wider as summer goes on and snow bridges weaken, so stay roped an

routes.name: Frostbite Ridge
routes.descent: Frostbite Ridge is essentially a one-way, committing line — once on the ridge there is no turning back — and virtually all parties descend a different, easier route rather than reversing the ridge. The standard descent is down the Sitkum Glacier: from the summit, descend the gully east of the summit into the upper Sitkum Glacier, traverse and descend to a saddle at roughly 8,000 ft, then continue

routes.name: Kennedy Glacier
routes.descent: Besides reversing the ascent line, the standard alternate descent goes via Frostbite Ridge: traverse past the distinctive 'Rabbit Ears' rock formation, then descend the (separate) Vista Glacier back down to the lower Kennedy Glacier and Kennedy Ridge camp, watching for opened crevasses and softening snow bridges throughout.

routes.name: Sitkum Glacier
routes.descent: This is a walk-off/glacier descent with no rappelling — reverse the ascent line. From the summit, descend the pumice Sitkum ridge back to the ~9,500 ft saddle east of Sitkum Spire, then descend the Sitkum Glacier's upper section, staying in the corridor left of the icefall/rock rib that splits the glacier's lower half, back down to Boulder Basin. Crevasses exist on the Sitkum but are sparse and ge

routes.name: East Face
routes.descent: The snow couloir on Golden Horn's east side belongs to the approach: from the ridge above Snowy Lakes it drops to the foot of the east face and is easy going with crampons and an axe. It is not the way off the route, so work out the descent from the top before committing to the face.

routes.name: North Face
routes.descent: Descend the Southwest Route: a short rappel of about 40 ft off the summit block regains the ridge, then class 2-3 scree and talus on the southwest side lead back down to Snowy Lakes. From camp, retrace the PCT over Granite and Cutthroat Passes to Rainy Pass.

routes.name: Northeast Arête
routes.descent: The arete ends on the summit, and the way off is the standard Southwest Route. A short rappel of roughly 35 to 40 ft down the summit block, from slings in the notch between the summit pillars, returns you to the ridge; a 30 m rope is plenty. Below that, loose scree and talus on the southwest side leads back toward Snowy Lakes, and plunge-stepping makes it quick. From camp, retrace the Pacific Cres

routes.name: Southwest Route
routes.descent: From the summit, most parties make a single short rappel (roughly 40 ft; a 30m rope is plenty) off the summit block to regain the ridge, then downclimb/scramble class 2–3 scree and talus back toward Snowy Lakes — plunge-stepping the loose scree speeds this considerably. From camp, retrace the PCT approach back over Granite and Cutthroat Passes to Rainy Pass.

routes.name: West Ridge
routes.descent: Descend the West Ridge talus back to the Dumbell-Greenwood col, then carefully reverse the narrow connecting ledge around Dumbell's east face to the ~7,900 ft notch above the south-side gully. Downclimb the loose Class 2-3 gully/ledges back into upper Phelps Basin; on snow, plunge-stepping or glissading speeds this section when conditions allow. There is no rappel route commonly described for this

routes.name: Raven Ridge Traverse
routes.descent: From Hoodoo's summit, downclimb the easy scree/talus slope on the peak's flank back to the approach trail near Libby Lake, avoiding a reversal of the exposed ridge crest.

routes.name: Standard Scramble
routes.descent: The standard descent is a straight reversal of the ascent: back down the summit boulder field to the pass south of the summit, down the entry gully and boulder field to the old cabin, and out Libby Creek Trail No. 415 to the trailhead. This is a walk-off/scramble descent with no rappelling required (rappels: 0) — no ropes, anchors, or technical gear are needed on the standard route. Some parties d

routes.name: East Ridge
routes.descent: The East Ridge is one of the mountain's more reasonable descents — at least one documented party climbed the North Ridge specifically so they could descend this ridge. Reversing it means downclimbing sustained Class 4 on loose rock with big exposure, so carry enough slings and cord to leave rappel anchors on blocks where downclimbing is unattractive. There are no fixed anchors. If you approached f

routes.name: Nohokomeen Glacier and Headwall
routes.descent: There is no rappel line — the standard descent is to downclimb what you climbed, ideally in your own steps. Reverse the corniced summit ridge carefully, then face-in downclimb the headwall; parties that are not comfortable simul-downclimbing 50-60 degree snow lower each other off buried pickets on the steepest 100 m or so. Recross the bergschrund at the same bridge you used on the way up, and be a

routes.name: North Ridge
routes.descent: The recorded modern practice is to traverse over the summit and descend the East Ridge (Grade II, Class 4), which puts you back on the eastern side of the mountain. That means downclimbing sustained Class 4 loose rock with occasional improvised rappels off slung blocks — carry tat and a few nuts, since there is no fixed gear on either ridge. routes.name: Northeast Glacier
routes.descent: There is no published descent for this route. The realistic options are to reverse the glacier — which on steep, heavily crevassed ice means downclimbing and/or lowering with pickets and screws, and re-crossing the bergschrund — or to traverse to the East Ridge or North Ridge and descend that, both of which are Grade II Class 4 and were used as a descent line by at least one party (a 2006 party as

routes.name: South Face / Southeast Ridge
routes.descent: Most parties reverse the ascent line: from the summit, downclimb the southeast ridge back to the top of the south face, then pick a descent line of gray rock ribs and gully rather than the loose 'bowling alley' gully used on the way up — marker ducks placed on the ascent are commonly used to relocate the correct line. The crux is getting back down through the cliff band via the hidden chimney and

routes.name: Southeast Ridge (Direct)
routes.descent: The practical descent is the South Face. From the summit, reverse the short summit ridge and work down the face's gullies and ribs, aiming for the notch in the south ridge and then for the slung boulder that sits above the hidden chimney in the lower cliff band. Rappel the chimney (25-30 m), reverse the left-slanting ramp and the rising scree traverse east, and regain the 7,000-7,200 ft southeast

routes.name: Southwest Ridge
routes.descent: Downclimb the Class 4 ridge, building rappel anchors on slung blocks where downclimbing is unattractive - there is no fixed gear and no established rappel line, so carry tat and a few nuts. Once back at the notch, reverse the ridge crest to Little Jack, then descend the Little Jack Trail 6.0 miles to the East Bank Trail junction and out to the highway. The descent is long rather than technical, an

routes.name: Southwest Gully
routes.descent: Descend by reversing the ascent line: downclimb the Southwest Gully's Class 3 loose scree, staying left/west of the waterfall low in the gully, back to the ridge saddle/bench, then pick your way down scree to Ragged Ridge Camp. From camp, reverse the roughly 6,600-6,800 ft sidehill traverse (crossing back over the stream/waterfall bench beneath Mesahchie Peak) to regain the base of Easy Pass, clim

routes.name: Southwest Slopes / Gully
routes.descent: Reverse the ascent line: downclimb the summit gully back to the ~7,400 ft bench, then work back east along the south-slope traverse, staying on or near the outbound line (cairns mark the route in places) to bypass the Grotesque Gendarmes buttress (a short 4th-class downclimb with real exposure) before regaining the sidehill traverse back toward Easy Pass and the maintained trail. This is a walk-of

routes.name: North Ridge
routes.descent: Downclimb the ridge crest back around The Smokestack via its west-side gully, return to the Klawatti-Austera Col, then to Klawatti Col. From there re-cross the Inspiration Glacier to the notch on Eldorado's East Ridge, descend the Eldorado Glacier, and follow the climbers' trail to the trailhead.

routes.name: Southeast Face / Klawatti Glacier
routes.descent: Descend by reversing the ascent line back down to Klawatti Col rather than continuing over the top on a different line. From the summit, downclimb the moderate 40-55° snow/ice slope back to the top of the short low-5th-class rock step that clears the bergschrund near the route's base. Multiple trip reports (including a 'white-knuckle' late-day retreat in worsening weather) describe this step being

routes.name: Klawatti Peak SW Buttress
routes.descent: Either reverse the ascent line, or descend north through a gully toward a rock feature known as The Smokestack, circle it clockwise to grassy ledges, descend the north ridge to the Klawatti Glacier, and follow glacier travel to the McAllister Glacier rappel station. Fixed anchors on the lower buttress allow three short rappels on the way down, though only the last one, onto the snow, is really nee

routes.name: Standard Scramble
routes.descent: This is a scramble, not a technical climb — there is no rappelling on the standard route (0 rappels) and no fixed anchors to look for. The normal descent is to reverse the East Ridge: downclimb the Class 2-3 granite back toward the lake basin, staying well clear of the steeper north wall and northeast face, which are notably steeper and not part of the standard line. routes.name: Wilkes-Booth (Northwest Face)
routes.descent: Descend the southwest face route: roughly 2,000 ft of steep snow and ice up to 65°, downclimbed in good conditions and otherwise rappelled. Below the face, traverse back along the north side of the peak toward Heliotrope Ridge, roped for the glacier, and walk out the Heliotrope Ridge Trail.

routes.name: X Couloir (Southwest Face) / Standard Route
routes.descent: Most parties reverse the ascent line, downclimbing and rappelling the same southwest gully/couloir system (the X Couloir) back down into the southwest basin below the face. routes.name: East Shoulder
routes.descent: Reverse the summit scramble carefully on the loose rock, then descend the glaciers along the ascent track, watching for opening crevasses later in the season.

routes.name: Standard Scramble
routes.descent: This is a walk-off/downclimb scramble descent with no rappelling — reverse the Class 2 ridge scramble back over the false summits to the col near Point 8107, back along the connecting ridge to Pass Butte, and down to Butte Pass and camp. routes.name: East Slopes
routes.descent: Descend by reversing the ascent line. From the summit, downclimb the East Ridge scrambling back to the top of the short, steep rock step below it — parties describe this step as low Class 4 and sometimes icy/verglassed in an adjacent gully. routes.name: Southwest Slope - Southeast Ridge
routes.descent: From the summit, downclimb the class 3 section, re-cross the exposed class 3+ traverse beneath the summit, and descend the class 2 south-face ledges back to the ridge and basin below. From there retrace the sheepherder's-trail traverse back through Luahna, Clark, and Boulder basins to the high camp, then follow Boulder Creek and the White River Trail back to the trailhead.

routes.name: West Ridge
routes.descent: Reverse the ascent line down the west ridge, following cairns back through the loose gully sections. The fixed rappel anchor near the summit allows a short rappel past the crux Class 4 step for parties who don't want to downclimb it; the rest of the descent is downclimbed. Expect the same loose-rock hazard on the way down as on the way up.

routes.name: Southwest Scramble
routes.descent: This route's crux move is on the ridge itself, not a technical descent: from the ridge crest (reached via the ascent line west of the Prong), drop roughly 70 vertical feet off the crest and wrap around to the south side of McClellan Peak, then scramble up class 3 rock to the true summit. Descend by reversing this exact sequence: downclimb the class 3 south-side rock back to the ~70-ft notch below

West Ridge / Southwest Gully
routes.descent: Standard descent is to reverse the ascent line: follow the exposed ridge crest back to the top of the west gully, downclimb the gully (steep Class 3/4 at its base) to Mesahchie Col, then reverse the slabs and the crest of the shoulder between Mesahchie and Katsuk down to the basin below the col. From camp, retrace the sidehill traverse, crossing the waterfall on the same bench near 6,500 ft, back

routes.name: Standard Scramble
routes.descent: This is a walk-off — there is no rappelling on the standard scramble route. Reverse the ascent line: downclimb the Class 3 (occasionally 3-4) rock/talus off the summit block to regain the south/southeast ridge at roughly 6,900 ft, then descend the left-angling ramp system back into Lower Monument Basin, topping off water at the lake-outlet creek if needed, before climbing back up to the Lake Mount

routes.name: Avalanche Glacier
routes.desc: A steeper, more direct way to the summit of Mount Adams than the popular South Spur, climbing straight up the Avalanche Glacier through some moderate ice sections.
routes.descent: From the summit, descend south via the South Spur snowfields (or the snowfield adjacent to the Avalanche/White Salmon glaciers) back toward the Morrison Creek/Cold Springs approach, glissading where conditions allow.

routes.name: North Face of the Northwest Ridge
routes.desc: Northwest Ridge is an intermediate Grade II ice and snow route on the north side of Mount Adams. More aesthetic than South Spur with less crowding. Moderate snow and ice climbing with good views.
routes.descent: Descend along the North Ridge to the Adams Glacier basin high camp, or in ski-descent conditions the route itself can be down-climbed/skied, threading the same rock-band pinch encountered on the ascent.

routes.name: Adams Glacier
routes.descent: This is a serious, committing route, not a car-to-car day climb for most parties — plan on a night at High Camp before the climb, then descend all the way to the car on summit day. The Adams Glacier line tops out on the upper mountain near the North Ridge/Suksdorf area close to the true summit (12,276 ft) rather than requiring a full crater traverse. Nearly all parties descend via the North Ridge

routes.name: Avalanche-White Salmon Glaciers
routes.descent: Climb out onto the summit plateau and head for the true summit, then descend the South Spur: cross the crater rim past Pikers Peak and follow the broad snow slopes of Crescent Ridge down to the Lunch Counter flats, where glissading is common on soft snow. From there the South Climb Trail runs down the old roadbed to Cold Springs, so no shuttle is needed if you started there. Going back down the Wh

routes.name: Lava Glacier Headwall
routes.descent: Descend the North Ridge back toward High Camp, the same non-technical but tedious scree/boulder walk-off used for the Adams Glacier and Lyman Glacier routes on this side of the mountain — long, loose volcanic scree, some narrow/exposed sections, and rockfall risk onto other parties, but no rappelling required on the standard line. From High Camp, retrace the High Camp Trail and Killen Creek Trail

routes.name: Lyman Glacier
routes.descent: Standard descent is the North Ridge (also called the North Cleaver) or the adjacent snowfield beside it, dropping back toward High Camp — this is a walk-off/downclimb, not a rappel route. It is the least pleasant part of the trip: long stretches of loose, rotten volcanic scree and boulders, occasional narrow/exposed sections, and a real chance of rockfall onto parties below, so groups should sprea

routes.name: Mazama Glacier Headwall
routes.descent: Reverse the ascent: back down the glacier past Sunrise Camp and out the way you came in to Bird Creek Meadows. Descending the South Spur instead is possible, but it is not a variation on the same day out - it finishes at the Cold Springs / South Climb trailhead on the mountain's south side, reached by an entirely different road system from the Yakama Nation approach this route starts on, so it onl

routes.name: North Ridge
routes.descent: Most parties descend the route itself, back down the North Ridge toward high camp; it is non-technical, mostly Class 2 over loose volcanic scree. Some parties instead carry over and descend the South Climb to Cold Springs, which requires a long car shuttle. Watch crevasses on any glacier descent. On the way down in early July, staying on the crest line, which cairns mark, is easier than dropping o

routes.name: North Ridge (West Face)
routes.descent: Descend the North Ridge, also called the North Cleaver, back toward High Camp. This is a walk-off over loose volcanic scree and boulders and is longer than it looks from above, with a real chance of knocking rock onto parties below, so spread out and move quickly through the worst sections. A rock band on the ridge can be downclimbed, and a short rope-assisted step is sometimes used by parties une

routes.name: South Climb (South Spur)
routes.descent: Retrace the ascent line: cross back over the shallow summit crater, down over Piker's Peak, and descend the broad snow slopes of Suksdorf/Crescent Ridge to Lunch Counter, then follow the old roadbed back to the trailhead. Glissading is common on the lower snowfields in firm-but-soft conditions; watch for exposed rock and runout hazards in late season as snow recedes.

routes.name: Wilson Glacier Headwall
routes.descent: The descent reverses back down the South Climb to Cold Springs: after topping out via the headwall, parties traverse over toward the summit plateau and descend the standard South Climb route (non-technical snow/scree walk-off, good glissading in early season) back to Lunch Counter and out to the Cold Springs trailhead — a different, easier line than the ascent. This is a walk-off, not a rappel des

routes.name: Boulder Glacier
routes.descent: Reverse the route: from the summit plateau go back down the Boulder Glacier past the crevasses on the upper glacier, whose bridges soften in the afternoon, and down the cleaver to the high camp on Boulder Ridge (about 5,700 ft, or a flat spot near 7,500 ft under the cleaver). Near the base of the ridge a short steep step, often protected with a fixed line, is downclimbed or rappelled. From camp, f

routes.name: Boulder–Park Cleaver
routes.desc: A moderate alpine snow route offering a quieter alternative to the heavily trafficked Coleman-Deming. The climb follows the Boulder–Park Cleaver across relatively crevasse-free terrain with multiple summit options: moderate snow slopes, 4th class rock north of the buttress, or a north-edge snow/ice slope. Earlier in season the terrain is less broken.
routes.descent: Reverse the cleaver and the lower Boulder Glacier crossing back to the 5,700 ft camp, downclimbing the class 3 step where the fixed line was left, then follow the Boulder Ridge Trail back to the trailhead; expect rockfall exposure near the 9,300 ft buttress on the way down as well as up.

routes.name: Coleman–Deming Glacier
routes.descent: This is a walk-off, not a rappel descent - reverse the ascent line. From the summit plateau, descend the Roman Wall carefully (many parties down-climb facing in on the steepest section, especially if icy or in a whiteout), back onto the Deming Glacier, across the Baker-Colfax saddle, and back down the Coleman Glacier icefall to the Hogsback and high camp. routes.name: Coleman Headwall
routes.descent: Descent is via the standard Coleman-Deming route, not back down the headwall, and it is a non-technical walk/downclimb with no rappelling required. From the summit plateau, drop down the Roman Wall — a ~35-45° snow slope that most parties downclimb or glissade in a boot-ski — to the saddle between the Black Buttes and Baker's summit dome. From there continue down onto the lower Coleman Glacier, ro

routes.name: Coleman Ski Descent
routes.descent: Ski or walk off by the way you came up. From the summit plateau drop down the Roman Wall, a snow slope of 35 to 45 degrees that is usually downclimbed or skied with care when it is icy, onto the Deming Glacier. routes.name: Easton Glacier
routes.descent: Non-technical walk-off: reverse the ascent line. From the summit plateau, descend the Roman Wall - a sustained 35-45 degree snow/ice slope that is the crux of the whole route and can be quite icy and rockfall-prone late season; many parties face in and plunge-step or down-climb it carefully - then back down the Easton Glacier to Sandy Camp/high camp, generally retracing the up-track and staying ri

routes.name: North Ridge
routes.descent: The North Ridge is climbed as an ascent-only line - parties do not reverse it. From the ridge crest, 2.5 to 6 belayed pitches of 60-85 degree alpine ice (hardest near the bottom, closer to WI2-3, easing higher) lead up past a prominent ice cliff/ice bulge around 9,600 ft, the route's steepest and most technical section, then the angle eases onto the upper ice cap; trend climbers' left (east) throu

routes.name: Park Glacier Headwall
routes.descent: Reverse the ascent: descend the Park Glacier, recross the Rainbow Glacier to camp near the Portals, then walk back along Ptarmigan Ridge to Artist Point, taking the lower line north of Coleman Pinnacle to avoid regaining height. Going down the Coleman-Deming instead ends at Heliotrope Ridge on the far side of the mountain and needs a car shuttle.

routes.name: Squak Glacier
routes.descent: From the summit, descend the upper mountain via the Easton route, then rejoin the Squak Glacier's descent line back past Sherman Peak to Crag View camp and the trailhead.

routes.name: East Face
routes.descent: Retrace the route; descend the green slot carefully and keep to the forest on the left on the way down to avoid the alder.

routes.name: South Slopes
routes.descent: Descend the south slopes, retracing the ascent into the basin.

routes.name: Standard Scramble
routes.descent: Reverse the route. The south and southeast gullies and slopes below the summit are loose gravel and slab: in mid June a slab layer slid free near 7,400 ft, and in August the gully south of the top was slow going. Descend one at a time and do not stand below a partner.

routes.name: Tribute to Richard
routes.descent: There is no rappel descent and no need for one. From the top of pitch 4 you are standing on the summit ridge; coil the ropes, stow the rack, and walk north a short distance to the true 8,449 ft summit. To get down, retrace the standard scramble line: from the summit, drop southeast and then east down the slopes and gullies that stay right (south) of the prominent rock wall you just climbed — do no

routes.name: South Slopes Scramble
routes.descent: Reverse the route. In late June the lower descent toward the river from the col was brushy, worst at the very bottom, and the upper scree allowed quick boot-skiing that avoids the Class 3 bits.

routes.name: Standard Route / South Side
routes.descent: Descend by the same line: the loose South Ridge back down to the 8,260-ft notch, then downclimb the short crux gully (three accounts describe this as a Class 3-4 downclimb; short-rope or a single short rappel off a natural rock/boulder anchor is reasonable if the gully is wet, icy, or a party is uncomfortable downclimbing — trip reports from parties on Custer's south side describe a rap anchor slu

routes.name: Southeast Face / Leroy Basin
routes.descent: Descend the same line used on ascent — Fernow's summit sits atop a maze of loose gullies and there is no reliable shortcut. From the top, downclimb the class 4 (occasionally low 5th, but the harder moves can be sidestepped) summit block; some parties, especially in wet rock or with a less experienced group, sling a horn or block on the north side of the block for a quick single rappel instead of d

routes.name: South Face / Southeast Ledges
routes.descent: The standard descent reverses the ascent line rather than following a separate walk-off. From the summit, downclimb the cairned class-3 summit gully back to the ledge system, then reverse the exposed, loose class 3/3+ ledge traverse above the chasm back to the snowfield alcove — parties commonly keep the rope on and simul-climb this section for protection, especially with any snow on the ledges. W

routes.name: Northeast Face Direct
routes.descent: From the summit/north ridge, descend the South Route, class 3-4 scrambling with some rappels and snow traversal to the Spider-Formidable col (crossover saddle), then follow the Ptarmigan Traverse route back across the Middle Cascade Glacier and Red Ledge to the Kool-Aid Lake camp.

routes.name: Direct East Ridge
routes.descent: There is no shortcut off East Fury - everything is a reversal. From the summit downclimb the 350 ft of Class 3 south ridge to the boulders, keeping off the steep summit snowfield, then traverse right below the cliff band back across the flat upper Fury Glacier at about 7,750 ft. Climb the Class 3 gully back up to the ledge on the west side of Point 7,850, cross to the south side of the crest and d

routes.name: North Buttress
routes.descent: The buttress is an ascent line only; the standard exit is over the top and down the other side. From the summit, downclimb the summit snowpatch (about 300 ft, 40 degrees at the base to nearly 50 degrees at the top - protect it with flukes or pickets, with the strongest climber first on belay) onto the Southeast Glacier, then descend the S-shaped snowfield past the bergschrund near 7,900 ft, keepin

routes.name: Southeast Glaciers (Standard)
routes.descent: This is fundamentally a walk-off/downclimb along the ascent line, not a rappel-heavy route, though one short technical step is often rappelled. From the summit, reverse the steep snowfield on a running belay with flukes (take particular care on the upper, firmer section — crampon-balling on wet snow has been reported), then retrace the Southeast Glacier descent, working back around the bergschrund

routes.name: Megalodon Ridge
routes.descent: Descend the standard Mount Goode line: from the true summit, downclimb and traverse the connecting ridge/notch system toward Black Tooth Notch, the deep gap short of the summit block. This section is done in three single-rope rappels - the first drops fairly directly down the ridge crest, but the second and third are traversing rappels that trend skier's-right/rappeller's-left, so keep the rope's

routes.name: Northeast Face
routes.descent: The shared standard descent off Goode (used for this route as for the Northeast Buttress) is down the Southwest Couloir. From the summit ridge, downclimb/rappel a short sequence of stations to Black Tooth Notch — these first rappels trend more sideways/traversing than straight down, so expect some rope-snag risk and use care feeding rope; a single 60m rope is sufficient at every station. From the

routes.name: Southwest Couloir
routes.descent: Descend the same Southwest Couloir used on ascent, after rappelling into it from the summit. From the summit area, downclimb broad class 3-4 terrain in the couloir, staying alert for a band of more solid darker rock on the left side (locally called the 'black stairs') which offers cleaner downclimbing than the surrounding rotten rock; the couloir is otherwise loose and rockfall-prone, so groups sh

routes.name: Northeast Buttress
routes.descent: Descent is via the Southwest Couloir, downclimbed and rappelled from the summit ridge. The standard sequence is three rappels from the summit down along the ridge to Black Tooth Notch — the first rappel runs close to straight down the ridgeline, but the second and third are notably traversing (trending skier's right/rappeller's left), so there is real rope-snag risk and parties should watch their

routes.name: South Slope - South Face (Standard Route)
routes.descent: From the summit, descend the loose South Slope/South Face talus and scree, or drop via the Southwest Slope variant, which avoids some of the steeper upper rock ribs. Many parties traverse instead to the Lago-Carru col to tag Mount Carru before returning to camp rather than descending fully and re-climbing. The rock is loose throughout, so move carefully, stay spread out, and watch for parties belo

routes.name: Fremont Glacier
routes.descent: Descend by reversing the ascent line. From the summit, most parties can downclimb the exposed Class 3-4 summit tower and the U-notch below it with care (a belayed downclimb works for many groups), but this step is steep and exposed enough that some parties choose to rappel roughly 30-50 ft off the summit block down to the snow hogback at the glacier's upper edge rather than downclimb it with packs

routes.name: Banded Glacier
routes.descent: Reverse the route: descend the Banded Glacier, climb back over the col toward Fisher Creek, and hike back out over Easy Pass to the trailhead (or exit via the longer Thunder Creek Trail alternate if Easy Pass Trailhead is inaccessible).

routes.name: Douglas Glacier
routes.descent: Descend the Banded Glacier via the Banded-Douglas col to reach the Fisher Creek basin, or reverse the Douglas Glacier with care back toward Easy Pass. A short rappel from the false summit drops to the saddle before the final class 4 summit block.

routes.name: North Face
routes.descent: The North Face is not descended — after topping out on the summit ridge (9,082 ft), descend via the standard South Slopes / south ridge walk-off: down the south ridge and upper talus to about 7,700 ft, then southwest down broad open slopes to the 6,840 ft saddle. From there most parties drop back into Leroy Creek Basin to retrieve camp and reverse the Leroy Creek climber's path and Phelps Creek Tr

routes.name: Entiat Ice Fall
routes.descent: From the summit, descend via the South Ridge, which in good conditions takes only about 30 minutes from the summit back to the ridge/basin area, considerably faster than the ascent.

routes.name: Nothing Couloir
routes.descent: Descend the South Shoulder route, which pairs well with the Nothing Couloir's west-side approach to form a natural loop back down toward Leroy Creek Basin rather than reversing the climb.

routes.name: Central Mowich Face
routes.desc: Central Mowich Face offers two route variations on the northwest face of Mount Rainier. Route follows steep snow and ice sections on a north-facing glacier. Two main variations exist: Grade III (direct, snow-dominant) and Grade IV (ice-steep variation).
routes.descent: From Liberty Cap or the main summit, descend via Emmons-Winthrop to Camp Schurman, or via Disappointment Cleaver to Camp Muir, depending on party preference and conditions.

routes.name: North Mowich Headwall
routes.desc: North Mowich Headwall (Edmunds Headwall) is a steep Grade IV ice and mixed route on the north side of Mount Rainier. Features sustained steep slopes and narrow hourglass rock/ice section.
routes.descent: From Liberty Cap, cross to the main summit area or descend directly via Emmons-Winthrop to Camp Schurman.

routes.name: Bread Loaf
routes.descent: There is no descent in the alpine sense — this is a single boulder a few feet off an established loop trail. After bouldering, simply walk back out the way you came (or continue the loop in the other direction back to a trailhead), following the Silver Falls Loop/Eastside Trail. No rappelling, downclimbing exposure, or route-finding is involved.

routes.name: Curtis Ridge
routes.descent: Curtis Ridge tops out onto the upper mountain near the Winthrop/Emmons basin, and the standard descent is to continue over the summit area and down the Emmons-Winthrop Glacier route to Camp Schurman, then follow the established boot path down the Inter Glacier back toward Glacier Basin and out to White River. This is a walk-off/glissade descent, not a rappel descent — many parties glissade a subst

routes.name: Disappointment Cleaver
routes.descent: Disappointment Cleaver is climbed and descended on the same line — there is no rappelling on the standard route; it's a roped glacier walk-down with a stretch of steep, exposed boot-packing on the Cleaver's rock-and-scree rib itself (guide services sometimes place seasonal hand lines/pickets on the Cleaver, but there's no permanent fixed gear). From the crater rim, parties retrace the ascent line

routes.name: Edmunds Headwall
routes.descent: From Liberty Cap descend toward the summit and the Emmons-Winthrop Glacier to Camp Schurman and White River, or descend west-side glaciers toward Mowich; plan exit logistics.

routes.name: Emmons–Winthrop Glacier
routes.descent: The Emmons-Winthrop is climbed and descended on the same line — a glacier walk-down, not a technical descent, with no rappelling required on a normal season's route. From the summit, parties descend the broad upper Emmons slope back through 'the Corridor' to Camp Schurman; this upper stretch is the crux of the descent not technically but navigationally, since the glacier is heavily crevassed above

routes.name: Fuhrer Finger
routes.descent: Most parties go back down the finger early in the day, before sun and warming send rock and ice down it, and then retrace the approach across the Wilson Glacier and the Nisqually Glacier to the Nisqually Moraine and the Skyline Trail to Paradise. The other choice is a carryover: continue over the summit crater and descend the Disappointment Cleaver route to Camp Muir and the Muir Snowfield, which

routes.name: Fuhrer Thumb
routes.descent: Most parties descend the adjacent Fuhrer Finger or the upper Kautz and standard Disappointment Cleaver route back to Camp Muir and Paradise.

routes.name: Gibraltar Ledges
routes.descent: Most parties reverse the ledges to descend — this is a downclimb/walk-off, not a rappel descent, though the terrain is exposed enough that some parties choose to belay or protect short sections. One documented ledge-traverse variation includes a short (~20 ft) rappel off the back side of a rock feature climbers call 'the beehive,' but that's not part of the standard line and isn't needed on most a

routes.name: Ingraham Direct
routes.descent: From the crater rim descend the upper glacier and traverse onto the Disappointment Cleaver, following it down to the Ingraham Flats, then Cathedral Gap and the Cowlitz to Camp Muir; from Muir, plunge-step or glissade the Muir Snowfield to Paradise. Stay roped across all glaciated terrain. Reversing the steep Ingraham headwall is possible early when it is firm, but most parties prefer the Cleaver f

routes.name: Kautz Glacier
routes.descent: Descending the Kautz is a real technical descent, not a walk-off, and involves multiple rappels through the ice chute — typically two to five depending on conditions, ice quality, and rope length. From the top of Wapowety Cleaver, parties reverse the glacier line down through crevassed terrain to the top of the ice chute, then find easier ground to climber's-left/east to belay into the chute rathe

routes.name: Kautz Headwall
routes.descent: Descent is normally either back down the Kautz Glacier itself (the way you came) or a carryover down the Disappointment Cleaver route to Paradise. On the headwall's ice steps specifically, with 60m ropes two double-rope rappels plus some downclimbing are enough to get back down through the steepest sections to the base of the ice pitches — rappel anchors on the ice steps are typically ice (V-threa

routes.name: Liberty Ridge
routes.descent: Liberty Ridge is never descended — its loose rock, sustained steep ice, and total lack of rappel anchors or safe bivy terrain below Thumb Rock make down-climbing the ridge far more dangerous than continuing up and over the mountain; the route's accident history is dominated by a dangerous pattern: parties judge that continuing up feels safer than retreating. From the summit area, the standard desc

routes.name: Mowich Face
routes.descent: There's no walk-off back down the Mowich Face itself — after topping out, the standard descent is a long carryover, either down the Emmons-Winthrop Glacier to Camp Schurman/White River, or down the Disappointment Cleaver to Paradise, both ending on the far side of the mountain, so arrange transport from there before you start. This is a walk-off/glacier descent, not a rappel descent; no fixed rapp

routes.name: Nisqually Icefall
routes.descent: This is a walk-off/downclimb, not a rappel descent. Two options are used: descend the Gibraltar Chute directly back toward Paradise — a direct, mostly non-technical line, though much of the chute is exposed to rock- and icefall so it's not necessarily the 'easy' option it sounds like — or carry over and descend the Disappointment Cleaver route (also to Paradise, same trailhead so no shuttle needed

routes.name: Ptarmigan Ridge
routes.descent: Ptarmigan Ridge is normally done as a carryover. Once on the summit plateau near the crater rim, descend the Emmons-Winthrop route: down the broad Emmons Glacier, threading its large crevasses, to Camp Schurman at about 9,500 ft. From the camp go around the south side of Steamboat Prow to Camp Curtis, descend the Inter Glacier, and follow the Glacier Basin Trail out to White River. Starting from t

routes.name: Sunset Ridge
routes.descent: The usual way down is over the top and down the Disappointment Cleaver, across to Camp Muir, then the Muir Snowfield to Paradise; this is a carryover, so leave a car at Paradise or arrange a shuttle back to the Westside Road. Early in the season, a party that camps on Puyallup Cleaver can instead descend the Tahoma Glacier, or its Sickle shortcut that skirts the crevasses of the main glacier, and

routes.name: Tahoma Glacier
routes.descent: Reverse the route, or descend toward the standard Disappointment Cleaver/Ingraham route and arrange a shuttle back to Westside Road; a documented recent trip logged about 8,770 ft of net descent loss over a 21.5-mile car-to-car itinerary starting from the Westside Road closure.

routes.name: Upper Castle Toprope Wall
routes.descent: As a toprope wall, there's no rappel involved in normal use — climbers are lowered off by their belayer after each route. If you need to walk to the top to rig anchors, the walk-off is a short scramble around the back/side of the formation back to the base trail; this is not described in detail anywhere, so treat it as a standard short crag walk-off and scout it before committing a party to the to

routes.name: Willis Wall
routes.desc: Willis Wall is a Grade V mixed alpine route on Mount Rainier's north face, between Liberty Ridge and Curtis Ridge, and ranks among the most intimidating alpine walls in the contiguous U.S. The wall features continuous mixed climbing on steep slopes between 45-60 degrees, with sustained rock and ice sections.
routes.descent: There is no descent route back down Willis Wall — after summiting, parties descend the standard Emmons-Winthrop Glacier route to Camp Schurman and out to the White River trailhead (the same drainage as the approach, reversing Curtis Ridge/St. Elmo Pass, or dropping directly to Camp Schurman and down the Inter Glacier to Glacier Basin and White River, glissading where snow allows). This is a walk-o

routes.name: South Face / Redoubt Glacier
routes.descent: Reverse the ascent line: downclimb or rappel the exposed Class 4 section from the summit horn back through the cannonhole, downclimb the loose gully/chimney system, and traverse back beneath the flying buttress to regain the notch at the head of the glacier. Rope up again for the glacier descent, then retrace the rock steps and slabs down to Ouzel Lake camp and follow the Depot Creek climbers' pat

routes.name: Fisher Chimneys
routes.descent: Reverse the ascent line in its entirety. From the true summit, downclimb the short 3rd/4th-class summit block to the head of the central gully, then descend via a mix of downclimbing and roughly two or three rappels off established stations — slung rock horns and existing fixed rings or webbing (inspect any tat before trusting it, and be ready to back it up) — to the base of the summit pyramid. A

routes.name: Hanging Glacier
routes.descent: From the summit, most parties tie into the same descent used off Price Glacier and the standard Sulphide route: downclimb/rappel the summit pyramid's gully system (natural horn-and-sling anchors, occasionally pickets — typically 1–3 short rappels on a single 30–60 m rope, condition-dependent) down to Hell's Highway (a ~60 m steep snow/ice step) and onto the Sulphide/Upper Curtis Glacier. Because t

routes.name: North Face
routes.descent: Climb over the summit and descend by Hell's Highway, the Upper Curtis Glacier, Winnie's Slide and the White Salmon Glacier back toward the ski area, rather than reversing the steep north face.

routes.name: Northeast Ridge
routes.descent: Standard descent is via the Fisher Chimneys line — down across the Upper Curtis Glacier, then Winnie's Slide and the chimneys themselves to the Lake Ann basin — or reverse the White Salmon Glacier.

routes.name: Northwest Arete
routes.descent: Descend the summit pyramid by its central gully on the south side, then follow the Fisher Chimneys descent: down Hell's Highway onto the Upper Curtis Glacier and across to the top of Winnie's Slide. Descend Winnie's Slide (steep snow, occasionally icy enough to rappel) to the head of the White Salmon Glacier, then go down the glacier as directly as the crevasses allow to the lower White Salmon Gla

routes.name: Price Glacier
routes.descent: The standard descent is NOT back to the Ruth Creek car — it's over the top and down the Fisher Chimneys to Lake Ann, a completely different trailhead. From the summit pyramid, downclimb and rappel the gully system on the pyramid's south side: climbers typically make 1–3 short rappels off natural anchors (slings on rock horns, occasionally pickets left in snow — don't count on finding a picket anch

routes.name: Sulphide Glacier
routes.descent: Descend the same line: reverse the Sulphide Glacier back to camp, then the Shannon Ridge Trail back to the trailhead. Off the summit, the standard descent down the central gully of the summit pyramid is a mix of downclimbing and rappelling. NPS climbing rangers have reported parties periodically replacing worn rap rings and anchors in the gully, so expect a mix of fixed rings/webbing at establishe

routes.name: White Salmon Glacier
routes.desc: Easy snow approach via White Salmon Glacier. Straightforward glacier climb with minimal technical difficulty. Gains roughly 7,500 ft car to car.
routes.descent: Downclimb the glacier back through Hell's Highway, across Curtis Glacier, down Winnie's Slide, and out around the clearcut to the White Salmon pull-off.

routes.name: Southeast Ridge (SE Corner)
routes.descent: Rappel the same 4th-class gully used as the standard ascent line up the summit pyramid (the line shared with the Fisher Chimneys/Sulphide Glacier finish); a 60m rope reaches all belay stations.

routes.name: SW Couloir and Face
routes.descent: Descend as for the Fisher Chimneys route, via the Hourglass and Upper Curtis Glacier to the Shuksan Arm; round trip from Lake Ann is roughly 8 hours.

routes.name: Silver Glacier
routes.descent: From the summit, down-climb the short Class 4 step to the sub-summit notch (~8,500 ft), re-cross the Silver Glacier (roping up as on the ascent) back down through its flat section to about 7,400 ft, then either return to the Custer-Spickard saddle (7,380 ft) and descend the wide gully to camp at Ouzel Lake, or drop north from the glacier toe over moraine and round the lake to camp at Silver Lake.

routes.name: Southwest Route / Silver Lake
routes.descent: The standard descent simply reverses the ascent line - there is no separate descent route and no rappelling on the Southwest Route. From the summit, downclimb the short scree chute and traverse back across to the east side of the crest, then reverse the short section of Class 2-3 gullies, chimneys, and rock ribs down to the notch/col on the southwest ridge. From the col, downclimb the short, steep

routes.name: Monitor Ridge
routes.descent: Descent is the same Monitor Ridge line back to timberline and then the Ptarmigan Trail back to Climbers Bivouac — there is no rappelling on this route (0 rappels; it is entirely a walk-off/scramble descent). The critical descent hazard is at the top: the crater rim is corniced with wind-built overhanging snow/ice that has repeatedly broken away, including a fatal collapse and multiple large rim fa

routes.name: Worm Flows
routes.descent: This is a walk-off/glissade descent with no rappelling — reverse the ascent line down Worm Flow Ridge, following cairns and wands (and wooden posts once below ~4,800 ft) back through the Worm Flows lava fields to treeline, re-cross Swift Creek above Chocolate Falls, and follow Swift Creek Trail #244 back to Marble Mountain Sno-Park. When snow conditions allow (typically most of the winter/spring s

routes.name: Gorillas Direct
routes.descent: Follow the West Ridge to the summit, or descend via the main gully with scrambling and downclimbing, breaking right on a large bench with a single-rope rappel option, before reaching Stuart Pass bivy sites.

routes.name: King Kong - Gorillas Direct Direct
routes.descent: Quickest descent follows the main gully of the West Ridge via scrambling and downclimbing before breaking skier's right onto a large bench with a single-rope rappel option, then downclimbing to bivy sites at Stuart Pass.

routes.name: Cascadian Couloir
routes.descent: Standard descent is simply reversing the ascent line — a walk-off/downclimb with no rappelling (0 rappels). From the false summit (~9,200 ft), descend the broken class 2-3 ridge back to the couloir, then work down the Cascadian Couloir itself, staying on the established climber's-left talus path around the permanent snowfield near 8,800 ft (parties who wander onto the right side of the snowfield h

routes.name: Girth Pillar
routes.descent: The route tops out on easier ground above the pillar, leading to the false summit above the Ice Cliff Glacier and on to Stuart's true summit. There is no reasonable way to reverse the route — down-climbing or rappelling back through the Ice Cliff Glacier's icefall and crevasse hazard is considerably more dangerous than finishing over the top, so continuing to the summit is effectively mandatory. F

routes.name: Ice Cliff Glacier
routes.descent: Descend via the Sherpa Glacier, starting near the false summit (~8,200 ft), back down into the basin below the Sherpa and Ice Cliff glaciers, then retrace the approach to the Stuart Lake Trailhead. Do not down-climb the ice route.

routes.name: North Ridge (Complete)
routes.descent: Nearly all parties descend via the Cascadian Couloir on the mountain's south side — this is a walk-off/downclimb with no rappelling required (0 rappels) under normal summer conditions. From the true summit, downclimb steep snow or scree, keeping right through sparse trees to drop into the head of the Cascadian Couloir, then follow the couloir down its full length (loose sand, scree, and rockfall-p

routes.name: Stuart Glacier Couloir
routes.descent: The couloir exits at or near the notch on the West Ridge, with a little more low fifth-class ridge to the summit. From the top, the usual way down is south by the Cascadian Couloir: cross the Class 2-3 ground between the true and false summits (steep, often corniced snow early in the season), drop into the couloir and follow it down loose scree and talus to Ingalls Creek, then regain Longs Pass an

routes.name: West Ridge
routes.descent: Descend via the Cascadian Couloir, the standard walk-off for the entire Stuart massif — this is a scramble descent, not a rappel route, under normal (dry to firm-snow) conditions. From the summit, reverse the short 3rd/2nd-class scramble east along the summit ridge to the false summit (~9,200 ft), then drop into the broken rock and scree above the top of the couloir. Stay climber's-right through s

routes.name: Always the Cowboy, Never the Cow
Sherpa Glacier
routes.descent: Early in the season the Sherpa Glacier itself is the best way down: reverse the roughly 40-degree snow of the couloir, facing in, back to the camp in the basin at its foot. When the snow is hard and icy this becomes a no-fall descent that may need rappels to reach the glacier safely, so carry pickets or other anchors and rope. Later in the summer, or if you are leaving the basin for the south side

routes.name: South Headwall
routes.descent: The route tops out very close to the true summit, so the way down is the Cascadian Couloir to the south. Cross the Class 2-3 ground between the true and false summits (steep, often corniced snow early in the season), then drop into the couloir and follow it down loose scree and talus to Ingalls Creek. The headwall base lies up-basin along the same drainage, so collect anything left there, then cli

routes.name: Upper North Ridge w/Great Gendarme
routes.descent: From the true summit, travel southeast on blocky 3rd/4th-class terrain toward the false summit, follow cairns down into the Cascadian Couloir snowfield, then descend extended 3rd-class scree/talus to Ingalls Creek. Sherpa Glacier or a Sherpa Pass glissade are faster early-season alternatives for parties returning to a north-side camp.

routes.name: Northwest Couloir (Cedar Creek approach)
routes.descent: From the summit, talus-hop back down the north ridge to the head of the couloir, then descend the snow by ski, glissade, or plunge-step depending on conditions and party equipment — one party describes boot-skiing scree to bypass icy sections before a long glissade/buttslide lower down where the slope softens and mellows. In mid-May, loose scree beside the icy slope lets you boot-ski down and skip

routes.name: Southwest Slopes / South Ridge
routes.descent: Descend by reversing the ascent line — there is no rappelling on this route. From the summit, retrace the south ridge/traverse back to Point 8,487, staying on the Class 1-2 line along or just below the crest (contour under the ridge horns rather than staying strictly on the crest). routes.name: Standard Route / Northwest Spire
routes.descent: Downclimb/reverse the ridge to the headwall, then rappel: parties commonly make several rappels down to the ridge's low point followed by a long double-rope rappel back onto Redoubt Glacier, then reverse the approach to camp.

routes.name: Southwest Slopes Scramble
routes.descent: Walk-off/downclimb — no rappelling on this route (rappels: 0). Descend the same southwest-ridge climbers' trail or south-face talus/scree line used on the ascent back down to Lake Doris camp (about 1,400 ft of descent, roughly an hour); the ridge line is preferred over the direct south-face boulder field for better footing, especially on wet rock. routes.name: Standard Scramble
routes.descent: Descend by reversing the ascent line: downclimb/scramble back along the Sawtooth crest talus to the saddle above Middle Oval Lake, then drop the scramble slope back down to the lake's outflow and rejoin the maintained Oval Creek Trail #410A. routes.name: Standard Scramble
routes.descent: No established alternate descent — down-climb/scree-descend the same south-slopes talus line used on ascent back to the high camp and drainage.

routes.name: East Slope
routes.descent: From the summit, downclimb the East Ridge back to Lucky Pass and descend the same eastern-margin line on the Borealis Glacier used on the ascent, staying off the central icefall. There is no established rappel line; parties without a rope can generally walk this off in good conditions, but carry a rope/pickets in case of deteriorating snow bridges.

routes.name: North Ridge
routes.descent: Because the crux notch has no fixed anchors and downclimbing loose 4th/5th class terrain is far riskier than climbing it, parties should plan to descend via the East Ridge to Lucky Pass and down the Borealis Glacier's eastern margin, even if they climbed the North Ridge to get up.

routes.name: South Ridge / McAllister Glacier
routes.descent: Descend by reversing the ascent line: down-climb the summit talus back to the North Klawatti Glacier, rope back up, and re-cross the glacier (same crevasse-probing caution as the approach) to the base of the McAllister-Klawatti notch. routes.name: Standard Scramble
routes.descent: This is a walk-off/scramble descent with no rappelling anywhere on the route (rappels: 0). routes.name: Southeast Ridge (Crater Lake Approach)
routes.descent: From the summit, downclimb the boulder scramble back to the ~8,000 ft col, then descend into the Crater Lake basin. In the one documented winter ascent, the party skied this descent back to a camp at Crater Lake before skiing/hiking out the following day via the unplowed Crater Creek Road.

routes.name: Raven Ridge Standard Route (Libby Lake Gully-Ridge)
routes.descent: There is no separate descent line for the standard route — parties reverse their ascent. The crux of the descent is the loose gully: move deliberately, stay to the climber's-left (looking downhill) on more solid rock where possible, and be conscious that dislodged rock can strike other parties below. routes.name: NW Ridge
routes.descent: From the summit, downclimb the upper ridge scrambling to the first gendarme, rappel its west side, continue down the ridge to the second gendarme, rappel it, then scramble down and around the west slope on boulders and scree, bypassing the North Summit, back to the high camp at ~7,500 ft; from there retrace the bushwhack to Remmel Lake.

routes.name: Southeast Slope (Standard Route)
routes.descent: Downclimb the talus/meadow boot path back to the Coleman Ridge Trail junction near 7,070 ft, then follow the trail back to Four Point Lake (or, via the Andrews Creek line, back down the Class 3 gullies or around via the Coleman Ridge contour) and out the approach trail to the trailhead.

routes.name: Standard Scramble
routes.descent: Descend by reversing the ascent line — there is no rappelling on the standard route. Downclimb the class 2–3 summit rocks back to the saddle/notch on the east ridge, then descend the scree, talus, and snow gully back into the SE basin at ~5,500–5,700 ft. routes.name: Southeast Ridge
routes.descent: From the summit, reverse the ridge scramble south-east along the crest back to the gap, downclimb the scree slope to the tarn basin, then follow the boot path/open slopes back down to the Beauty Creek tributary crossing (~5,200 ft) and down the steep, brushy Beauty Creek Trail to its junction with the Robinson Creek Trail. routes.name: South Slopes via Emerald-Saska Col
routes.descent: Descend the same col traverse and basin scree. In early-to-mid season, continuous snow below the col allows a glissade or boot-ski descent; by August-September this becomes loose scree and dirt requiring slow, controlled steps rather than good scree-skiing. routes.name: Northeast Couloir
routes.descent: Most parties reverse the couloir (downclimbing or rappelling the snow/ice) back to the approach path. An alternative used by some parties is to traverse to Sherpa Pass and downclimb from there to regain camp, avoiding a full re-descent of the steepest snow.

routes.name: East Ridge
routes.descent: Most parties do not reverse the East Ridge; the accepted descent is to finish near the summit, traverse to the top of the West Ridge, and go down using the West Ridge's established rappel line (two single-rope rappels past the crux, a short scramble, another single, then a double-rope rappel to the west notch - see the West Ridge descent for full detail) before dropping back to the basin and Ingal

routes.name: North Ridge
routes.descent: Descent is not a reversal of the North Ridge and is considered the trickiest part of the route. From the summit, downclimb/scramble a short distance to an established rappel station just west of the true summit - the top anchor of the standard West Ridge route - and make a short rappel (roughly 25-30 ft/one short pitch) down into a gully southwest of the summit. routes.name: West Ridge
routes.descent: The standard descent reverses the West Ridge using a sequence of rappels rather than downclimbing the whole route. From the summit area, two single-rope rappels lead down past the crux (5.4-5.6) pitch to a short 3rd-class scramble; this is followed by another single-rope rappel and then a longer double-rope rappel (two ropes joined, or a single 60m doubled) that returns you to the west notch below

routes.name: East Ridge
routes.descent: From the summit, rope down or downclimb a short distance to gain the Silver Star Glacier, then descend the glacier west/northwest toward Burgundy Col. From the col, climb/hike up and over to the Burgundy Col climbers' trail, which drops back to Highway 20 near milepost 166 (roughly 4 miles from Washington Pass) — several miles of highway from the Cedar Creek Trailhead used for the approach. routes.name: Silver Star Glacier
routes.descent: Descend by reversing the ascent route. From the summit, downclimb the short class 3–4 rock (the same easy, somewhat exposed ledge system used on the way up) back to the col between the east and west summits; several trip reports and topo photos document a natural/slung rappel anchor near the true summit that parties use to bypass the most exposed section of this downclimb — a single rappel with on

routes.name: Northeast Ridge
routes.descent: Reverse via the glacier and Burgundy Col.

routes.name: Northwest Face
routes.descent: From the west summit, join and follow the Silver Star Glacier descent line back over Burgundy Col and down the standard approach trail to Highway 20.

routes.name: West Face Couloir
routes.descent: From the west summit, traverse/descend to join the Silver Star Glacier route and follow it back over Burgundy Col to the approach trail.

routes.name: North Face
routes.descent: Most parties downclimb the moderating upper snow slopes and pick an easier walk-off line (often via the west ridge) rather than reverse the full face; the line has also been skied. Return via the Chickamin and Dome Glaciers to Itswoot Ridge and out the Bachelor Creek/Downey Creek trails.

routes.name: Southwest Route
routes.descent: Reverse the ascent line. Most parties downclimb the same loose south-side gully back to the Dome–Sinister col — it is one of the loosest, most unpleasant sections on the mountain, so expect care-intensive downclimbing with real rockfall risk to anyone below.
