routes.name: Neve Glacier / Standard Route
routes.descent: Descent reverses the ascent line rather than following an independent route. From the summit, downclimb the exposed class 3 (occasionally low class 4) notch and gully back down to the rocks above the Neve Glacier, then retrace the glacier crossing - roped, watching for crevasses and softening snow bridges later in the day - back up to the Colonial-Neve col. routes.name: West Ridge (Beckey Route)
routes.descent: Descend by reversing the ascent line rather than any independent walk-off. From the true summit, most parties make three single-rope (30 m) rappels down the tower to a small, exposed high notch, then one longer double-rope (60 m) rappel from that notch down into the gully/glacier below — roughly four rappels in typical late-summer, snow-free conditions. routes.name: The Devils Club
routes.descent: The East Face is rappelled top to bottom on its own line — there is no walk-off, and no fixed/bolted rappel stations exist anywhere on the route; every anchor is natural (slung horns, chockstones/gear anchors) built on the spot, so a party needs full natural-anchor-building skill and a rack sufficient to leave gear behind. routes.name: West Route
routes.descent: There is no rappelling on this route and no shortcut descent gully — it is a walk-off and downclimb by the line used on the ascent. routes.name: Northwest Ridge
routes.descent: There is no established descent for this route. The options are either downclimbing/rappelling the ridge back toward Fish Creek Pass on the loose rock encountered on the way up, or, if terrain and party skill allow, working across to the easier Southwest Spur/scramble line used by the standard route and walking off to Star Lake before returning to the pass. routes.name: Standard Scramble
routes.descent: This is a walk-off/downclimb — no rappelling on the standard Southwest Ridge scramble route. From the summit, reverse the ridge scramble back down to the head of the scree slope, then descend the same loose scree/talus line back into the Star Lake basin. routes.name: Southwest Scramble
routes.descent: Descent reverses the ascent line. From the notch/crack area just below the true summit, most parties downclimb the ~15-ft crux crack and the exposed Class 4 ledge just below it. Some instead rappel off the fixed slings (in-situ tat/webbing — inspect it and back it up before committing) back to the ledge on the north side; even with a 60 m rope, expect to downclimb some Class 3 terrain. routes.name: Southwest Route / Standard
routes.descent: Descend by reversing the ascent line — this is a walk-off/downclimb with no rappelling required (rappels: 0). From the summit, downclimb back through the broken rock to the ridge notch, then follow the ramp/ledge system down the climber's-right side of the main gully, retracing the zigzag line back past the cave and reddish boulder, and back across the talus field to the Snowy Lakes camp. routes.name: East Face
routes.descent: Downclimb the summit pitch and upper class 4 terrain back through the ledge system, taking care around the crux flake/crack; parties have used a 30 m rope for the technical sections. Continue down the zigzagging ledges and the lower class 2-3 ramp back to the basin below the face, then reverse the cross-country traverse over the pass above Bird Lakes to Company Creek Trail.

routes.name: Standard Route (South Ridge / South Gully via Copper Glance Basin)
routes.descent: From the summit, downclimb the south ridge back into the gully/chute and descend the loose scree and talus to the upper basin. Where snow remains, an ice axe (and crampons/microspikes if firm) is useful, and glissading the snow sections can speed descent when conditions allow. routes.name: Windy Peak via Iron Gate Trailhead (Boundary Trail / Sunny Pass Approach)
routes.descent: From the summit, retrace the Windy Peak Trail east to the Sunny Pass junction, then follow the Boundary Trail south back down to the Iron Gate Trailhead.

routes.name: Windy Peak Trail (Standard Walk-up)
routes.descent: Reverse the ascent trail (out-and-back). A loop via the Iron Gate/Horseshoe Basin trail system is possible instead of retracing the Long Swamp trail, but requires a car shuttle or significant extra road walking.

routes.name: Windy Peak via Windy Creek Trail (Cathedral Driveway Approach)
routes.descent: From the summit, downclimb the short Class 2 scramble to rejoin the trail, then descend the Windy Creek Trail back to the Cathedral Driveway trailhead — watch for the trail junction where this route splits from the Long Swamp approach.
